### [`v4.131.0`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/HEAD/packages/wrangler/CHANGELOG.md#41310)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/compare/wrangler@4.130.0...wrangler@4.131.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​15480](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15480) [`36aed7f`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/36aed7f0f2db5056af9df917cf6c22a2be950b1e) Thanks [@​skepticfx](https://redirect.github.com/skepticfx)! - Add Durable Object-managed Containers to top-level container configuration

  Wrangler now accepts `scheduling_policy: "durable_object"` in the top-level `containers` array and creates its namespace-backed application after the Worker upload resolves the Durable Object namespace ID. The namespace ID is also the application ID, so repeated deploys idempotently ensure the same application without name-based lookup, modification, or a Containers rollout.

  Durable Object-managed entries accept `class_name`, `scheduling_policy`, an optional `name`, and an optional named `images` map. Scheduler-only fields are rejected. Each image provides either a local `dockerfile` or a digest-pinned managed-registry `image`. Wrangler builds or resolves each image, waits while Cloudflare prepares it for the Containers runtime, and uploads the resulting references with the Worker version for access through `ctx.container.images` and `env.EXPERIMENTAL_CLOUDFLARE_CONTAINER_IMAGES`. Local development support for these entries is deferred to a follow-up.

  Existing scheduler-backed entries and Durable Object migrations continue to work unchanged.

  With `--containers-rollout=none`, existing Workers retain their deployed Container metadata and image binding even when local `containers` is omitted or empty; local scheduler edits are also ignored. The upload stops if the deployed versions cannot be recovered. Existing Workers for Platforms dispatch scripts reject this flag before upload because their API does not expose enough metadata to preserve Container associations safely. First deployments can still skip Container preparation and rollout. Without this flag, removing managed Containers, including by omitting `containers` entirely, clears the experimental image binding even with `keep_vars`.

  `versions deploy` validates the selected versions before changing traffic and creates their Durable Object-managed applications only after deployment succeeds. Both `deploy` and `versions deploy` report partial completion if application creation fails afterward, with instructions to retry the same command.

  `EXPERIMENTAL_CLOUDFLARE_CONTAINER_IMAGES` is a temporary, reserved Wrangler binding until native Container image metadata is available. Its class keys identify managed applications during `versions deploy`, including classes with empty image maps. User configuration cannot declare a binding with this name; existing versions that already use it are treated as Container configuration.

- [#​15493](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15493) [`493e635`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/493e63548f75f8f1d9847f5576835e2e1f1682a5) Thanks [@​GregBrimble](https://redirect.github.com/GregBrimble)! - Remove `wrangler preview settings` commands

  The private-beta `wrangler preview settings` and `wrangler preview settings update` commands are no longer available.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​15411](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15411) [`0b43395`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/0b433956a805d7aa86b39ebffc2c2d476a40cc89) Thanks [@​xgame92](https://redirect.github.com/xgame92)! - Fail `wrangler versions upload` early when a Worker has a pending Durable Object migration

  Wrangler now directs users to run `wrangler deploy` to apply the migration instead of sending a version upload request that the API will reject.

- [#​15518](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15518) [`9d75006`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/9d75006728cb1f6a7df6b30cd7f80cc5194d5ad5) Thanks [@​taylorlee](https://redirect.github.com/taylorlee)! - Detect named-only module Worker entrypoints correctly

  Wrangler now distinguishes named-only module Workers from legacy Service Workers that happen to have named exports. A default export identifies a module Worker; otherwise, legacy `addEventListener` registration identifies Service Worker format.

- [#​15581](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15581) [`b605aa6`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/b605aa60b4c9ed2546a0fd1a6ebc677c15422bc0) Thanks [@​MattieTK](https://redirect.github.com/MattieTK)! - Correct Pages-to-Workers delegation analytics for forced and ineligible commands

  The legacy `forced` result counted every agent-driven Pages command using `--force`, including commands that could never have been delegated. Wrangler now emits `eligible_forced` only when `--force` prevents an otherwise eligible delegation, and records other agent commands as `ineligible` with a bounded reason and whether force was used.

- [#​15432](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15432) [`f45b596`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/f45b5968bac153d6f436f8408968573aecb44a94) Thanks [@​razethion](https://redirect.github.com/razethion)! - Prevent delayed internal errors from fetch-only remote bindings

  Fetch-only remote bindings such as D1 and R2 previously opened an unused WebSocket RPC session. RPC sessions are now created only when an RPC method is called.

- [#​15585](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15585) [`f69f95a`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/f69f95aa2da329dcfa9888cfeb204cdda634d979) Thanks [@​dependabot](https://redirect.github.com/apps/dependabot)! - Update dependencies of "miniflare", "wrangler"

  The following dependency versions have been updated:

  | Dependency                                                               | From          | To            |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- | ------------- |
  | [@​cloudflare/workers-types](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-types) | ^5.20260908.1 | ^5.20260910.1 |
  | workerd                                                                  | 1.20260908.1  | 1.20260910.1  |

- [#​15554](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15554) [`bff525d`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/bff525d66dd3785481148353d782dd33c3a644ed) Thanks [@​XiaoZ-0218](https://redirect.github.com/XiaoZ-0218)! - Add the missing `transferred_classes` migration to the config schema

  `DurableObjectMigration` described `new_classes`, `new_sqlite_classes`, `renamed_classes` and `deleted_classes`, but not `transferred_classes`. `normalizeAndValidateConfig` has always validated that key, and the deploy path forwards it to the API along with the rest of the step, so Transfer migrations worked — but `config-schema.json` is generated from the type, so an editor resolving `$schema` reported a valid, documented migration as an unknown key.

  Adding the field to the type puts it in the generated schema. No runtime change.

- [#​15584](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15584) [`96688b3`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/96688b3ccada3b56ad6cc42e1cbd63f4c268db1a) Thanks [@​Svector-anu](https://redirect.github.com/Svector-anu)! - Bump `shell-quote` to 1.9.0+ to pick up two disclosed advisories

  `shell-quote@1.8.1` is affected by a ReDoS in `parse()` (CVE-2026-13311 / GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv — an unauthenticated attacker who can feed a string into `parse()` can block the event loop for tens of seconds with plain space-separated input, no shell metacharacters required) and by an object-token escaping bug in `quote()` (CVE-2026-9277 / GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p), both fixed upstream in `1.9.0`. Wrangler's `parse()` wrapper (`src/utils/shell-quote.ts`) is reachable from `pages dev`/`init` command-line parsing, so the ReDoS applies; the `quote()` call site only ever passes string arguments, so the object-token issue was not reachable here, but there is no reason to stay on a vulnerable range once a patch exists.

- [#​15563](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15563) [`ed5797a`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/ed5797a17d837c381ebb63f50ea3fdc155df88fe) Thanks [@​Bortlesboat](https://redirect.github.com/Bortlesboat)! - Encode filenames in Pages HTML redirects

  Fix `wrangler pages dev` returning a 502 response when redirecting HTML paths containing Unicode characters. Keep reserved characters in filenames encoded in the redirect destination and preserve the request query string.

- [#​14889](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14889) [`128235a`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/128235a8c08ca40d93b96d408297d21cbdcc9eb6) Thanks [@​chinesepowered](https://redirect.github.com/chinesepowered)! - Fix `wrangler types --strict-vars=false` emitting invalid TypeScript for an empty array var

  A var whose value was an empty array produced `()[]`, which is a syntax error. Because this lands in the generated `worker-configuration.d.ts`, it did not just break that one line — the whole file failed to parse, so no binding types resolved at all. An empty array now generates `unknown[]`.

- [#​15494](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15494) [`f8aea7e`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/f8aea7e325357fc490c8f37dc2f750fe35dfd59e) Thanks [@​GregBrimble](https://redirect.github.com/GregBrimble)! - Use `previews_base_config` for Preview configuration

  Preview commands now read the Worker Previews Base configuration from the `previews_base_config` API field.

- [#​15569](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15569) [`24ef86b`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/24ef86ba87da44cda2ae4cc42b5cb57dc5ff6669) Thanks [@​RealBhupesh](https://redirect.github.com/RealBhupesh)! - Fix `wrangler workflows instances describe` crashing on dynamic retry delays

  The Workflows API serializes function retry delays as `"[dynamic]"`. The describe command previously parsed that as a duration, produced an Invalid Date, and threw `RangeError: Invalid time value` before printing remaining steps. It now renders `unknown (dynamic delay)` and also tolerates attempts whose `end` timestamp is missing.

- Updated dependencies \[[`f45b596`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/f45b5968bac153d6f436f8408968573aecb44a94), [`f69f95a`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/f69f95aa2da329dcfa9888cfeb204cdda634d979), [`a549e58`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/a549e58af707e84d6aeddaadc6566103ae236dbb), [`dbb3ff4`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dbb3ff4ebe7579be76f42591957c429f26da319b), [`fea3cd0`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/fea3cd0f2ef5af6c8f2b50c794a89b8ef03ca82b), [`6bd7b6c`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/6bd7b6cae44d441e415130991e3f181694bd3b6d), [`15cd6e1`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/15cd6e16129af3dad09d53d6cd03f963f9203970), [`be1caec`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/be1caeca44ccd9660a81420805fb0958ca422589), [`dbc9506`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dbc9506e48d99237be701685d08582966f62f59f)]:
  - <miniflare@5.20260910.0-alpha>

### [`v4.130.0`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/blob/HEAD/packages/wrangler/CHANGELOG.md#41300)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/compare/wrangler@4.129.1...wrangler@4.130.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​14372](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14372) [`dbf6aad`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dbf6aad7b85fad3a2848191804bf627c591b5821) Thanks [@​ichernetsky-cf](https://redirect.github.com/ichernetsky-cf)! - Add `containers[].observability` support to `wrangler deploy`

  Wrangler now accepts container-specific observability settings via `containers[].observability`, including application-level targeting fields for Containers. Root `observability` continues to work as a fallback when a container does not define its own observability settings.

  `wrangler deploy` now preserves legacy `configuration.observability` for existing container apps that still use rollout-based observability, while using top-level application observability for new or already-migrated apps.

  Existing application diffs are now normalized even when stored resource limits cannot be mapped to a named instance type. API-only metadata and equivalent managed-registry image names no longer appear as edits or affect whether deployment changes require a rollout.

- [#​15004](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15004) [`e20df20`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/e20df2042a73fc6d861f07113efc5804b4c0a119) Thanks [@​MattieTK](https://redirect.github.com/MattieTK)! - Delegate agent Pages project creation with a production branch to Workers

  When run by an AI agent, `wrangler pages project create --production-branch <name>` is now eligible for delegation to a Workers static-assets deploy. The production branch names the target that a Workers deploy would publish to, so it does not need to disqualify a brand-new project from delegation.

  `wrangler pages deploy --branch <name>` remains on Pages because an interactive new-project flow separately prompts for its production branch. The deployment branch may therefore represent a preview and cannot safely be converted into a production Workers deployment.

- [#​15004](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15004) [`e20df20`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/e20df2042a73fc6d861f07113efc5804b4c0a119) Thanks [@​MattieTK](https://redirect.github.com/MattieTK)! - Widen agent Pages-to-Workers delegation to new projects on accounts that already use Pages

  When run by an AI agent, `wrangler pages deploy` and `wrangler pages project create` now delegate a brand-new static Pages project to a Workers static-assets deploy even when the account already has other Pages projects. The gate is now per-project rather than per-account: a command targeting a project that already exists stays on Pages, but a new project is delegated regardless of the account's other Pages projects.

  A project name restored from the Pages configuration cache is only used when the cache belongs to the currently authenticated account. An account-matching cached name remains on Pages even when the project is missing remotely, preserving the user's recorded Pages intent. After switching accounts, an otherwise unnamed deploy stays on Pages rather than treating a stale cached project name as a new project on the selected account.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​15560](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15560) [`edb3631`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/edb3631666677b51d58000d23ed693d83da9ff48) Thanks [@​dependabot](https://redirect.github.com/apps/dependabot)! - Update dependencies of "miniflare", "wrangler"

  The following dependency versions have been updated:

  | Dependency                                                               | From          | To            |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- | ------------- |
  | [@​cloudflare/workers-types](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-types) | ^5.20260907.1 | ^5.20260908.1 |
  | workerd                                                                  | 1.20260907.1  | 1.20260908.1  |

- [#​15557](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15557) [`63c7ff1`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/63c7ff17b3ac5ca0b977297456fe3bcbe71e90f4) Thanks [@​tomekancu](https://redirect.github.com/tomekancu)! - Fix `wrangler d1 execute --local` being extremely slow with large SQL files or commands

  The local SQL splitter consumed quoted strings and comments character-by-character, re-checking the full accumulated string each time. This made splitting a large quoted value or comment quadratic, so seed files could take tens of seconds to run. The splitter now only inspects a bounded trailing window on each step, making splitting effectively linear. The remote path is unaffected as it imports the file server-side.

- [#​15542](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15542) [`a4e41df`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/a4e41df43cc93686bf57a16b1de0a4b06860f2b9) Thanks [@​NAVEENKUMARKR777](https://redirect.github.com/NAVEENKUMARKR777)! - Fix `wrangler dev` running the custom build command twice on startup and on every config change

  Wrangler already runs the custom `build.command` once before starting `wrangler dev`, to resolve the Worker's entry point. When `dev.watch` wasn't explicitly disabled, `BundlerController` then unconditionally ran the same build command again the moment it started watching for changes, and repeated this on every subsequent config reload too.

  For fast build commands this just meant duplicate log output (e.g. a `vite build` visibly running twice at startup). For slower or stateful build commands, running two builds concurrently against the same output files could corrupt the result or fail outright (for example, non-deterministic `wasm-opt` failures have been reported for Rust builds).

  The initial watcher setup now only bundles the output the build command already produced, instead of re-running the command. Real file changes detected by the watcher still re-run the build command as before.

  Wrangler now ignores broken-pipe errors from stdout and stderr while preserving the existing failure behavior for other output errors.

- [#​14001](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/14001) [`c0c6504`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/c0c650424c983c02de8ed008d3de0eb90cdc2396) Thanks [@​for-the-kidz](https://redirect.github.com/for-the-kidz)! - Update bundle size warning thresholds to use uncompressed size instead of gzip size

  The compressed script size limits (3 MiB free / 10 MiB paid) have been removed server-side in favor of a single 64 MiB uncompressed limit. The bundle size reporter now compares the uncompressed bundle size against this 64 MiB limit for its color-coded warnings, instead of comparing gzip size against the old 3 MiB compressed limit.

- [#​15499](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15499) [`ffc7efd`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/ffc7efdc93b09a6345ecb7073ed56731d439e6fc) Thanks [@​WillTaylorDev](https://redirect.github.com/WillTaylorDev)! - Honor Workers Builds name overrides in `wrangler preview`

  Preview commands now target the Worker name supplied by Workers Builds instead of the name in local Wrangler configuration. This prevents preview builds from failing when the two names differ.

- [#​15252](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15252) [`682cd44`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/682cd44fcd18940e143b2c63bb7ebf17f3254531) Thanks [@​GregoryCollett](https://redirect.github.com/GregoryCollett)! - `wrangler dev` no longer exits when a request to your Worker fails transiently

  Previously, a transient network failure on a single request — most commonly a request arriving just as an idle internal connection was closed, after roughly five seconds without traffic — could take down the whole dev server with an empty `✘ [ERROR]`, leaving the port unbound until restarted. In CI test suites, one such failure caused every remaining test to fail with connection errors.

  `wrangler dev` now automatically retries the affected request if it is safe to repeat (GET and HEAD requests). If a request still fails, it fails individually — the error is logged with the request method and URL — and the dev server keeps serving.

[If a trait item appears in rustdoc search, hide the corresponding impl items](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145898). Previously a search for "last" would show both `Iterator::last` as well as impl methods like `std::vec::IntoIter::last`. Now these impl methods will be hidden, freeing up space for inherent methods like `BTreeSet::last`. - [Relax rules for identifiers in search](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/147860). Previously you could only search for identifiers that were valid in rust code, now searches only need to be valid as part of an identifier. For example, you can now perform a search that starts with a digit. ## Compatibility Notes - [Fix backtraces with `-C panic=abort` on Linux by generating unwind tables by default](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/143613). Build with `-C force-unwind-tables=no` to keep omitting unwind tables. * As part of the larger effort refactoring compiler built-in attributes and their diagnostics, [the future-compatibility lint `invalid_macro_export_arguments` is upgraded to deny-by-default and will be reported in dependencies too.](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/143857) * [Update the minimum external LLVM to 20](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145071) * [Prevent downstream `impl DerefMut for Pin`](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145608) * [Don't apply temporary lifetime extension rules to the arguments of non-extended `pin!` and formatting macros](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145838) ### [`v1.91.1`](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/HEAD/RELEASES.md#Version-1911-2025-11-10) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/compare/1.91.0...1.91.1) \=========================== - [Enable file locking support in illumos](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148322). This fixes Cargo not locking the build directory on illumos. - [Fix `wasm_import_module` attribute cross-crate](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148363). This fixes linker errors on WASM targets. ### [`v1.91.0`](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/HEAD/RELEASES.md#Version-1910-2025-10-30) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/compare/1.90.0...1.91.0) \========================== ## Language - [Lower pattern bindings in the order they're written and base drop order on primary bindings' order](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/143764) - [Stabilize declaration of C-style variadic functions for `sysv64`, `win64`, `efiapi`, and `aapcs` ABIs](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144066). This brings these ABIs in line with the C ABI: variadic functions can be declared in extern blocks but not defined. - [Add `dangling_pointers_from_locals` lint to warn against dangling pointers from local variables](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144322) - [Upgrade `semicolon_in_expressions_from_macros` from warn to deny](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144369) - [Stabilize LoongArch32 inline assembly](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144402) - [Add warn-by-default `integer_to_ptr_transmutes` lint against integer-to-pointer transmutes](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144531) - [Stabilize `sse4a` and `tbm` target features](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144542) - [Add `target_env = "macabi"` and `target_env = "sim"` cfgs](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/139451) as replacements for the `target_abi` cfgs with the same values. ## Compiler - [Don't warn on never-to-any `as` casts as unreachable](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/144804) ## Platform Support - [Promote `aarch64-pc-windows-gnullvm` and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm` to Tier 2 with host tools.](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/143031) Note: llvm-tools and MSI installers are missing but will be added in future releases. - [Promote `aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` to Tier 1](https://redirect.github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145682) Refer to Rust's [platform support page][platform-support-doc] for more information on Rust's tiered platform support. ### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>astral-sh/uv (uv_build)</summary>

### [`v0.13.1`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0131)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/0.13.0...0.13.1)

Released on 2026-10-14.

##### Enhancements

- Ignore `Requires-Python` upper bounds in `uv pip check` and `uv pip install --strict`, consistent with resolution ([#​22500](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22500))
- Support Linux SPARC by falling back when filesystem cloning and detailed cache accounting are unavailable ([#​22463](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22463))
- Report missing trusted hashes in resolution errors ([#​22241](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22241))

##### Python

- Add CPython 3.16.0a1 ([#​22527](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22527))

##### Preview features

- Allow `uv tool upgrade` to upgrade installed tools when `tool-install-locks` is enabled ([#​22498](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22498))
- Add preliminary support for parsing PEP 825 variant labels in wheel filenames with `wheel-variants` ([#​22039](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22039))

##### Performance

- Reduce uv's binary size ([#​22429](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22429), [#​22430](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22430), [#​22432](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22432))
- Speed up Simple API parsing ([#​22429](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22429))
- Reduce package metadata parsing overhead ([#​22239](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22239))

##### Bug fixes

- Prevent tool and managed Python uninstalls from deleting unrelated files beside their storage directories ([#​22495](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22495))
- Restore support for source distributions containing hard links or full-length tar user or group names ([#​22516](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22516), [#​22522](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22522))
- Preserve device files and FIFOs used as `uv pip compile` or `uv export` output destinations ([#​22496](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22496))
- Fix `sys._base_executable` detection for environments created from symlinked interpreters ([#​22520](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22520))
- Prevent concurrent readers from observing partially written lockfiles, Python version files, or managed Python sysconfig files ([#​22399](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22399), [#​22402](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22402), [#​22403](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22403))
- Serialize concurrent project commands that reach the same environment through real and symlinked paths ([#​22390](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22390))
- Prevent installs, syncs, and environment creation from failing when they race with `uv cache clean` ([#​22387](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22387))
- Prevent concurrent tool installations from corrupting an environment when the last tool is uninstalled ([#​22391](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22391))
- Persist changed upgrade settings even when `uv tool upgrade` leaves the tool version unchanged ([#​22499](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22499))
- Reuse environments with installed Git dependencies pinned to full commit hashes without resolving again ([#​22464](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22464))

##### Documentation

- Explain how to select an emulated Python interpreter on Windows ARM64 when native wheels are unavailable ([#​22424](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22424))
- Fix the `.netrc` format documentation link ([#​22514](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22514))

##### Other changes

- Publish Python 3.15-based uv Docker images under stable tags ([#​22503](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22503))

### [`v0.13.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0130)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/0.12.24...0.13.0)

Released on 2026-10-09.

uv 0.13.0 makes Python 3.15 the default stable Python version. We've also included several breaking changes to improve correctness, performance, and compatibility, described below.

**We expect most users to be able to upgrade without making changes.**

While not a breaking change, this release also updates the format of many of uv's cache entries to improve performance. **uv may download or rebuild dependencies after upgrading**, because some cached entries from earlier versions cannot be reused. Multiple versions of uv can still safely share the same cache directory.

There are no breaking changes to the configuration of the [uv build backend](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/build-backend/). If your `[build-system]` table includes an upper bound on `uv_build`, update it to allow `uv_build` 0.13, e.g., `uv_build>=0.13.0,<0.14`.

##### Breaking changes

- **Use Python 3.15 as the default stable version**

  The default stable Python version has changed from 3.14 to 3.15. This affects Python downloads when no version is requested or pinned, e.g., when running `uv python install`.

  uv continues to use compatible Python installations that are already present. For example, `uv venv` can still use an installed Python 3.14. If no suitable interpreter is installed and automatic downloads are enabled, commands such as `uv venv` and `uvx python` can now download Python 3.15.

  You can opt out of this behavior by requesting Python 3.14 explicitly, e.g., `uv venv --python 3.14`. For projects, use `uv python pin 3.14` to record the version in `.python-version`.

- **Honor `--require-hashes` in included constraints files** ([#​22275](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22275))

  Previously, uv ignored `--require-hashes` in constraints files included with `-c` from a requirements file. Now, uv honors the directive and requires hashes for all requirements in the installation. Installs that previously succeeded can now fail if a requirement is missing a hash.

  You cannot opt out while the directive is present. Add the missing hashes to your requirements, or remove the `--require-hashes` directive from the included constraints file if hash checking is not intended.

- **Prefer native Python on Windows ARM64** ([#​22100](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22100))

  Previously, ARM64 builds of uv preferred emulated `x86_64` Python installations because native wheel support was limited. Now, uv prefers native ARM64 (`aarch64`) interpreters across Python versions.

  This follows similar changes in [CPython](https://discuss.python.org/t/python-on-windows-arm64/104524), the official Windows [Python install manager](https://discuss.python.org/t/python-install-manager-26-4/108846), and GitHub's [actions/setup-python](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python#supported-architectures).

  When a native interpreter is unavailable, uv continues to fall back to `x86_64`, then 32-bit `x86`.

  You can opt out of this behavior by setting `UV_PYTHON_ARCH=x86_64` or requesting an explicit architecture, e.g., `cpython-3.14-windows-x86_64`. If you are using `setup-uv`, you can set [`python-arch: x86_64`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv#python-architecture) instead.

- **Reject editable requirements in included constraints files** ([#​22282](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22282))

  Previously, uv silently ignored editable (`-e`) requirements in constraints files included with `-c` from a requirements file. Now, uv rejects these requirements with an error, matching [pip's behavior](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/#constraints-files).

  You cannot opt out of this behavior. Move editable requirements to a requirements file passed with `-r`, or pass them directly with `--editable`, instead of including them in a constraints file.

- **Omit the distutils startup patch on Python 3.10 and later** ([#​22096](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22096))

  Previously, uv installed `_virtualenv.py` and `_virtualenv.pth` into every new virtual environment to prevent distutils configuration from changing installation paths. Now, like [`virtualenv` 21.6.0](https://redirect.github.com/pypa/virtualenv/releases/tag/21.6.0), uv omits these files on Python 3.10 and later, which already ignore the affected configuration keys. This reduces Python startup overhead. Python 3.9 and earlier retain the patch.

  You cannot opt out of this behavior. Existing virtual environments are not modified automatically. Recreate an environment with Python 3.10 or later to remove the patch.

  This stabilizes the `no-distutils-patch` preview feature.

- **Treat requirement-file option values as single paths** ([#​22290](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22290))

  Previously, uv split values passed to `--constraint`, `--override`, `--exclude`, and `--build-constraint` on spaces, even when quoted. Now, each value is treated as a single path, allowing file paths containing spaces.

  You cannot opt out of this behavior. Repeat the option to provide multiple files. For example, replace `-c "a.txt b.txt"` with `-c a.txt -c b.txt`.

  Space-separated lists in `UV_CONSTRAINT`, `UV_OVERRIDE`, `UV_EXCLUDE`, and `UV_BUILD_CONSTRAINT` remain supported.

- **Use `tar-codec` for tar archives by default** ([#​22094](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22094))

  Previously, uv used `astral-tokio-tar` to extract tar archives, build source distributions with `uv_build`, and read their metadata for `uv publish`. Now, uv uses `tar-codec`, which applies stricter validation when reading archives.

  uv may now reject archives containing hard links or unsupported tar extensions that previous versions accepted. Source distributions created by `uv_build` can also have different archive bytes and hashes.

  You can opt out of this behavior by setting `UV_LEGACY_TAR_BACKEND=1`.

  This stabilizes the `tar-codec` preview feature.

- **Reject `uv build --clear` output directories that contain a build source**
  ([#​22276](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22276))

  Previously, `uv build --clear` could delete a project or input source distribution when the
  output directory contained the source. Now, uv rejects these output directories, including
  equivalent paths reached through symlinks, before clearing any build output.

  Select an output directory that does not contain any build sources, or omit `--clear`.

##### Python

- Add CPython 3.15.0 ([#​22400](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22400))

##### Preview features

- Require hashes for build dependencies, including transitive dependencies, with `--require-build-hashes` ([#​21411](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21411))

##### Performance

- Speed up revalidation of cached HTTP responses by avoiding rewrites of unchanged payloads ([#​22130](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22130))
- Reduce allocations when reading cached HTTP responses ([#​22136](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22136))
- Reduce cache storage for HTTP policies and package records ([#​22135](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22135), [#​22133](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22133))
- Reduce allocations for cached source distribution revisions ([#​22131](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22131))

##### Bug fixes

- Fix incorrect dependency resolution when reusing source metadata with different build settings ([#​22404](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22404))
- Avoid overlong wheel cache lock filenames on Windows ([#​22134](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22134))

</details>

### [`v10.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v10.3.0): 🌈 Add Python architecture selection

pulls.title: [ty] Infer nested classes as read-only attributes
pulls.body:
Allow a subclass to override a nested class with a subclass of that nested class, such as `Child.Meta` inheriting from `Base.Meta`. Treat nested class declarations as read-only attributes so writes through a base-typed reference cannot invalidate the subclass's narrower type.

Direct access on the outer class literal (e.g. `Base.Meta`) retains the exact class object. Access through an instance or `type[Base]` exposes `type[Meta]` instead, accounting for possible subclass overrides. Apply this contract to attribute overrides, protocols, and metaclasses, while allowing explicit instance annotations to redeclare inherited nested classes as writable attributes.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4711.

## Test plan

Compared Rust type layouts before and after widening `TypeQualifiers` to `u16` on aarch64, with debug assertions enabled and disabled. The layouts of `TypeAndQualifiers`, `PlaceAndQualifiers`, and `ProtocolMemberData` were unchanged, so the expansion of `TypeQualifiers` fits into existing padding, it doesn't actually cost memory.

## Ecosystem report

Compatible nested-class overrides are accepted, while incompatible overrides retain errors with updated class-object type displays. Instance reads expose existing dynamic-base limitations in Alerta and remove a strict redundant-condition warning in Spack. Freqtrade’s removed override error follows existing gradual assignability for unknown ancestry.

Analyzed head `de50d5e915679c63dfe06ce4d2df99a7f6740577`; [full ecosystem report](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29346#issuecomment-6172170919).

pulls.title: [ty] Fix attribute writes through type variables
pulls.body:
Attribute writes through a bounded or constrained type variable can accept a value that only some possible receivers support, or reject valid writes when the same attribute is instance storage on one receiver and a descriptor on another. Resolve each receiver's write and delete contract independently instead of combining its raw member types first.

Preserve the original type variable when binding `Self` in attribute annotations, property setters, protocol members, and `__setattr__`. Each receiver uses the normal attribute-write resolution, including custom setters and frozen-class restrictions.

Preserve the outer slot descriptor during cycle recovery so recursive slotted attributes retain their inferred storage type and normal attribute checking.

## Ecosystem report

The ecosystem changes follow the stronger receiver checks: class replacement preserves `Self`, constrained writes check every receiver, and a valid property write is accepted. Two existing errors change wording. Spack’s dynamic-base relationship and httpx-caching’s client/transport correlation remain existing analysis limitations exposed by the stricter checks.

Analyzed head `7c3e62388c0210b680190ab1e05cada6be824d62`; [full ecosystem report](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29345#issuecomment-6172169833).

pulls.title: [ty] Filter incompatible union members during union inference
pulls.body:
When solving an assignability check against a target union type, we currently recurse into `infer_map_impl` before verifying assignability. This can allow constraints derived from incompatible union elements to remain as inference evidence, leading to incorrect inference results.

```py
from typing import Any, Callable, Protocol

class HasMethod(Protocol):
    def method(self) -> int: ...

def f[T](callback: Callable[[T], None], value: T, other: Any | HasMethod) -> T:
    return value

def accepts_object(value: object) -> None: ...
def _(other: object):
    reveal_type(f(accepts_object, 1, other))  # main: object, now: Literal[1]
```

Note that this affects the legacy solver path, which should be removed after https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/3557, but this fixes a few false positives in the meantime.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve shared structure in ambiguous overload return types
pulls.body:
When gradual arguments leave multiple overloads applicable, ty can lose useful information by collapsing the entire return type to `Unknown`. For example, receiver overloads returning `Series[Timestamp]` and `Series[Timedelta]` produce `Unknown` for a `Series[Any]` receiver.

Preserve shared return-type structure and replace only differing parts with the existing overload-ambiguity marker. The example now produces `Series[Unknown]`, retaining member checking on the returned container. This applies recursively to matching generic classes, tuple shapes, and `type[...]`, including through recursive aliases. Other structural differences fall back to `Unknown`.

Compare all remaining return types together so equivalent types with different representations cannot make the result depend on overload declaration order. Overload applicability and argument expansion continue to use the existing selection rules.

Closes astral-sh/ty#4055.

## Ecosystem report

Verified head [`d32af57e`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/commit/d32af57e7774744bba2e5b425b186106f4d4b1b1) against the [fresh ecosystem run](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/actions/runs/38585724938). Its 441 retained diagnostic changes match the previous analysis, apart from an upstream Scrapy line shift. The documented pre-existing checker and stub limitations remain unchanged; no new ecosystem finding was introduced by these comment and mdtest updates. Full analysis and reproduction provenance: [part 1](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29342#issuecomment-6158340152) and [part 2](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29342#issuecomment-6158339795).

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve receiver checks for aliased methods
pulls.body:
Currently some synthesized methods handle `Self` differently than normal methods: instead of treating `Self` as an inferrable typevar in the generic context of the synthesized methods, they eagerly replace `Self` with the concrete defining class.

The code implementing this eager substitution was a little too broad, and could also catch method aliases, in cases like this (real-world example):

```py
from collections.abc import Awaitable
from typing import Any, Literal, Protocol, overload, reveal_type

class AsyncClient(Protocol):
    _is_async_client: Literal[True]

class SyncClient(Protocol):
    _is_async_client: Literal[False]

class Commands:
    @overload
    def incrby(self: SyncClient, name: str) -> int: ...
    @overload
    def incrby(self: AsyncClient, name: str) -> Awaitable[int]: ...
    def incrby(self: Any, name: str) -> int | Awaitable[int]:
        raise NotImplementedError

    incr = incrby

class Redis(Commands):
    _is_async_client: Literal[True] = True

def f(r: Redis) -> None:
    reveal_type(r.incrby("k"))  # Awaitable[int]
    reveal_type(r.incr("k"))  # expected Awaitable[int]
```

On main, we incorrectly categorize the `incr` alias as a synthesized method, so we prune overloads correctly for `r.incrby` calls but not for `r.incr` calls.

This PR makes `Self` handling consistent across synthesized and normal methods, which fixes these calls to method aliases, too. 

Synthesized named-tuple and dataclass methods now register `Self` in their generic contexts and connect field annotations to that inferable type variable. This lets them use ordinary call inference too, removing the synthesized-method exception from receiver binding. Specialized protocol receivers and constrained receivers retain their existing handling.

Pydantic constructor receivers are positional-only, matching the runtime signature and keeping fields named `self` separate from the receiver.

Fixes astral-sh/ty#4715.

## Test plan

Ran the classmethod, constrained-TypedDict, and union-receiver examples from the review of #26861 against this implementation. Aliased classmethods preserve their return types and subclass `Self`; constrained TypedDict subscription is accepted; the invalid union-receiver call retains `no-matching-overload` diagnostics instead of becoming non-callable.

## Ecosystem report

Analyzed [`4e13215104`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/commit/4e13215104f9168c581c2c52236082be0a47b26a). Most changes update existing receiver counts; alias inference becomes more precise and borrowed methods enforce their receiver constraints. Additional errors expose documented existing binding and generic-inference limitations. All changes are accounted for, with no unresolved blocker for this PR. [Full ecosystem analysis](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29341#issuecomment-6157452697).

pulls.title: [ty] Optimize system path equality
pulls.body:
## Summary

This PR makes borrowed `SystemPath` equality cheaper by comparing the underlying paths with `std::path::Path::cmp(...).is_eq()`. Camino's `Utf8Path` equality instead calls `Iterator::eq` on its components, so it parses both paths component by component and bypasses the standard library's comparison fast paths. `Path::cmp` first scans matching bytes: identical paths return immediately, while differing paths resume component comparison at the preceding separator. This avoids parsing the long matching paths repeatedly encountered in file-database lookups.

Camino already used this component-by-component equality in [February 2021](https://github.com/camino-rs/camino/blob/c7b26958e30e0fd456f7a73de11a03f85267f943/src/lib.rs), before Rust [added the shared-prefix optimization in August 2021](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/86898), so their implementation didn't inherit that later optimization.

The comparison retains component equality: `a/b`, `a//b`, `a/./b`, and `a/b/` remain equal, while leading `./` and unresolved `..` components remain significant. Hashing continues to delegate to `Utf8Path`, so borrowed lookups remain consistent with `SystemPathBuf` keys. No filesystem access or canonicalization is involved.

(The choice of `cmp` is workload-dependent. The standard library's `Path::eq` compares components from the end, which can reject different filenames quickly; `cmp` benefits our frequent successful lookups. Rust disables the shared-prefix shortcut for Windows drive and UNC prefixes and falls back to component comparison, so these results do not establish the same speedup on Windows. Delegating comparisons upstream in Camino is also worth investigating; it already adopted a [similar optimization for hashing](https://github.com/camino-rs/camino/pull/120).)

Whole-project Callgrind runs show 10.08% fewer instructions on one OpenAI application and 0.34% fewer on a second application, with byte-identical diagnostics and exit status. The number of file lookups and path comparisons is unchanged; the gain comes from cheaper comparisons. These are workload-specific instruction-count reductions, rather than a general wall-clock speedup.

pulls.title: [ty] Centralize child-region inference and result merging
pulls.body:
## Summary

This change extracts common entry points for inferring child regions and incorporating their results into the surrounding inference. Child regions are parts of a scope, such as definitions and expressions, whose types can be inferred and cached independently.

This prepares for the on-demand reaching-definitions lookup in #29247. The lookup can identify which definitions can supply a name's value using the same inference logic and cached type results, without storing reaching definitions in the type-inference cache. This change also extracts the scope selection used by complete-scope inference.

## Approach

When inferring a scope, the builder can use a cached child result without visiting the child's expressions itself. For example:

```python
old = 1
new = old
```

The builder can reuse the cached inference for the definition of `new`, without visiting the `old` expression in the scope builder. [`infer_and_extend_definition`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/dc30229d0372b73346bf508bc1b183cc5940051d/crates/ty_python_semantic/src/types/infer/builder.rs#L592) now groups the child query and the merge of its results. In #29247, this entry point also runs the same inference builder on the child with name-resolution recording enabled. This records `old = 1` as a reaching definition of `old` while continuing to use the cached type result.

The other entry points apply the same pattern to statements, expressions, nested scopes, deferred definitions, function defaults, and decorators. [`complete_inference_scope`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/blob/dc30229d0372b73346bf508bc1b183cc5940051d/crates/ty_python_semantic/src/types/infer.rs#L495) extracts the existing choice of an enclosing scope when a lambda or comprehension needs its type context. The follow-up lookup uses the same choice to start inference with the right context.

## Test Plan

This is a behaviour-preserving refactor that relies on existing tests.

pulls.title: [ty] Refresh copied dependency directories in tests
pulls.body:
Updating `uv` to `0.13.0` in #29336 causes the external `attrs` and `numpy` mdtests to report unresolved imports even though their dependencies were installed successfully.

The external-dependency helper copies a real virtual environment's `site-packages` into the test database's in-memory filesystem. `Db::create_directory_all` creates directories without notifying the database. Copying Python files refreshes their immediate parent directories, but copying files nested inside packages can leave the cached state for the `site-packages` root stale. With `uv 0.12.23`, copying the top-level `_virtualenv.py` file incidentally refreshed that directory. The environments created here by `uv 0.13.0` omit that file, exposing the missing notification.

Call `File::sync_path` for the destination `site-packages` after copying finishes. This explicitly refreshes the directory state used by import resolution, making dependency loading independent of whether the environment contains any top-level Python files.

pulls.title: [ty] Deduplicate identical argument type diagnostics
pulls.body:
Unpacking a tuple with repeated incompatible element types into a variadic parameter can emit identical `invalid-argument-type` diagnostics at the same starred argument. Report each identical mismatch once, while retaining distinct errors for different source arguments, parameters, or expected and provided types.

Deduplicate when emitting diagnostics so all parameter matches, type checks, and failing-overload error counts remain intact.


## Ecosystem report

For head `ed5e760595e57b6f83c6bd66e9dbdc80d149fcad`, the ecosystem comparison removes three duplicate `invalid-argument-type` diagnostics: two in Prefect and one in SymPy. Each affected call retains one error, and distinct diagnostics remain unchanged. Exact-run reproduction and minimized examples confirm the expected behavior; all readiness checks passed.

[Full ecosystem report](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29337#issuecomment-6152510514).

pulls.title: [ty] Enable invalid-mutable-override by default
pulls.body:
## Summary

Enable `invalid-mutable-override` as an error by default. We now reject overrides that narrow a writable attribute's type without requiring users to opt in:

```python
class Base:
    value: int

class Child(Base):
    value: bool  # invalid-mutable-override
```

Code accepting a `Base` can assign any `int` to `value`, violating the subclass's `bool` annotation. The rule remains independently configurable, so users can disable it while migrating.

Addresses [the default-severity discussion in #28556](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28556#discussion_r4261238726).

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve minimum lengths of unpacked tuple unions
pulls.body:
Reject calls where every member of an unpacked tuple union supplies too many arguments once later positional arguments are included:

```python
def f(a: int) -> None: ...

def g(args: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int]) -> None:
    f(*args, 1)  # too-many-positional-arguments
```

Combining unequal tuple shapes previously discarded their minimum lengths, allowing argument matching to treat `args` as empty. `TupleSpecBuilder::union` now preserves the smaller minimum length when combining shapes, so `Type::iterate` retains that guarantee for all its consumers. This also preserves required elements when unpacking tuple unions into tuple literals or inferring a `TypeVarTuple`.

Addresses the [minimum-length review comment](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29293#discussion_r4248949931) on #29293.


## Ecosystem report

Analyzed head: [`1b5eb5424c`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/commit/1b5eb5424c7fad6edf6994d73a36691f358a97e2). [Full report](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29331#issuecomment-6150237369).

The five changes are understood and acceptable for this fix: two more precise Bokeh messages, two rewrites of existing Meson cyclic-inference warnings, and one duplicate SymPy argument error. No newly rejected calls were found. The duplicate reflects pre-existing reporting behavior for nonempty tuples and can be addressed independently.

pulls.title: [ty] Make override checker dispatch explicit
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now select signature or attribute override checking independently of diagnostic emission. Declared attributes use attribute compatibility, even when the overriding member is a method:

```python
from collections.abc import Callable

class Base:
    # An ordinary Callable attribute does not bind a receiver.
    f: Callable[[int], int]

class Child(Base):
    # Attribute checking compares (int) -> int with the bound method's () -> int.
    # This pair never enters the method checker, even when the error is ignored.
    def f(self) -> int:  # ty: ignore[invalid-attribute-override]
        return 0
```

Previously, a result of "no attribute violation" let execution continue into the method checker, conflating compatible overrides, unavailable attribute contracts, and pairs of methods. We now distinguish those outcomes explicitly and return attribute violations for separate reporting.

Signature checking still handles methods that replace inferred callable defaults. An unannotated assignment does not declare an attribute type, but its callable signature can constrain an overriding method:

```python
class Factory:
    def __init__(self, value: int) -> None: ...

class Base:
    make = Factory

class Child(Base):
    # Still invalid-method-override: the inherited callable accepts a value.
    def make(self) -> Factory:
        return Factory(0)
```

Methods replacing callable `Final` attributes also retain signature checking. Finality and signature compatibility are independent: suppressing or disabling either diagnostic leaves the other check enabled.

Missing or inactive declarations are skipped, so diagnostics name the ancestor that supplies the applicable contract. Ordinary method pairs are classified before constructing attribute contracts, and constructors retain their existing checks.

Follow-up to #29327.

pulls.title: [ty] Infer generic calls across positional unpack lengths
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now infer generic calls from complete arrangements of variable-length positional arguments. An empty `before` returns the integer list below; a one-element `before` returns a string list:

```python
def first[T](value: list[T], other: object = None) -> list[T]:
    return value

def call(before: list[list[str]], value: list[int]):
    result = first(*before, value)
    reveal_type(result)  # list[int] | list[str]
    result.append(1)  # invalid-argument-type
```

Each arrangement constrains all arguments together, including keyword arguments. We specialize the return type for each complete solution before combining the results, preserving both invariant containers and relationships between type variables.

Alternative matching is limited to scalar literals and references to already-typed values. Arguments that need contextual inference retain ordinary matching, as do constructor calls and calls with unresolved `ParamSpec` or `TypeVarTuple` parameters.

pulls.title: [ty] Respect suppression of attribute override diagnostics
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now allow a single ignore to suppress an incompatible attribute or property override:

```python
from collections.abc import Callable

class Base:
    # Callers can pass an int to this callable.
    f: Callable[[int], int]

class Child(Base):
    # This override is incompatible: the bound method accepts no arguments.
    # Before: ignoring invalid-attribute-override exposed invalid-method-override,
    # so suppressing the same conflict required a second ignore.
    # After: this ignore suppresses the conflict, with no further diagnostic.
    def f(self) -> int:  # ty: ignore[invalid-attribute-override]
        return 0
```

Previously, the attribute checker only told its caller whether it emitted a diagnostic. Suppressing that diagnostic therefore caused the caller to continue into the method checker, which reported the same conflict under a different rule. We now return the applicable rule even when its diagnostic is suppressed or disabled, so the method checker does not revisit that conflict.

Disabling an attribute or property override rule also avoids this fallback. We still check other base classes for violations of enabled rules.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4710.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve positional alternatives across constructor methods
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now preserve each valid arrangement of positional unpacks through a complete constructor call. For example, an empty `before` puts the integer list in `value`, while a one-element `before` puts a string list there:

```python
class Box[T]:
    def __init__(self, value: list[T], other: object = None):
        self.value = value

def create(before: list[list[str]], value: list[int]):
    box = Box(*before, value)
    reveal_type(box)  # Box[int] | Box[str]
    box.value.append(1)  # invalid-argument-type
```

Metaclass `__call__`, `__new__`, and `__init__` share the same choice of arguments and unpack lengths. We solve their shared class parameters together, apply defaults after collecting their argument evidence, and combine the resulting instance types. Every member of a tuple union must produce a valid complete call.

Expected return types can guide inference without discarding an otherwise valid argument placement. Deprecation warnings account for the completed constructor alternatives. A lone trailing variable-length unpack retains the existing element checks against optional parameters, including when it is part of a union.

Alternative matching is limited to scalar literals and references to already-typed values, including callbacks. Context-dependent arguments retain ordinary constructor matching and inference. Unsupported signatures and calls exceeding the existing expansion budget also retain their existing behavior.

pulls.title: [ty] Combine collection element types before solving constraints
pulls.body:
## Summary

Depends on https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29313.

We now join collection element types before adding inference constraints for unconstrained type variables. This collapses equivalent element types into a single bound, avoiding redundant solver comparisons for collections of many callables with the same signature.

Bounded or constrained collection type variables still check each element individually, including when a custom typeshed supplies those constraints. A benchmark covers a dictionary containing many lambdas with the same signature.

pulls.title: [ty] Bound recursive type and signature rendering
pulls.body:
Depends on https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29284.

Rendering a recursive type can revisit the same nested structure many times while preparing a diagnostic. Callable wrappers and temporary buffers can also reset the signature recursion guard, allowing deeply nested signatures to exceed the display limit.

We keep one rendering context across nested formatting and temporary buffers. Plain text and IDE labels share limits on nesting, work, and output size. When a limit is reached, we abbreviate a complete fragment and remove its navigation metadata together, retaining valid ranges for the remaining text. Name collection is bounded as well.

Each render starts with fresh state. Repeated sibling signatures still display in full, while recursive signatures retain their guard through wrappers, unions, and tuples.

pulls.title: [ty] Reuse inference results in union annotations
pulls.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #29304.

We reuse the results of ordinary annotation inference when extending a PEP 604 union. Each expression returns its annotation type, a normalization result from #29304, and an optional runtime value. The enclosing union can reuse these results for both ordinary classes and specialized generics; deferred annotations reuse normalization without performing runtime checks.

The annotation type and runtime value remain separate: `bool | int` simplifies to the annotation type `int`, while its value is still a union object. Runtime values stay within the current traversal and are reused only with matching inference flags and outside cycle recovery. The existing operator checks and intermediate expression types are preserved.

Regression coverage includes nested unions, custom metaclass operators, overloaded `TypeForm` calls, and incremental changes to operators and class bases.

## Performance

Compared with #29304, matched single-worker CLI checks on an Apple M5 Max with optimized dev builds reduce median instruction counts for 256-member annotation unions by 91% for ordinary classes and 94% for specialized generics. Deferred annotations improve by 94–95%. These are synthetic scaling cases; instruction counts across attrs, anyio, hydra-zen, and DateType range from −0.23% to +0.10%, with unchanged diagnostics. Each comparison uses one warmup and three interleaved measured runs.

pulls.title: [ty] Match variadic positional parameters across unpack lengths
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now consider alternative unpack lengths when a callable has a variadic positional parameter. A later argument can fill a named parameter while earlier and later unpacks fill the remaining positions:

```python
def f(a: str, b: str, c: float, *rest: str): ...

def call(args: list[str]):
    f(*args, 1.0)
```

The matcher checks a repeated segment's element type when it reaches the variadic parameter, preserving errors such as passing `list[str]` to `*args: int`. Successful placements also retain the information used to prefer variadic overloads. Generic calls preserve each complete return type when different placements infer different specializations.

Alternative matching is limited to scalar literals and references to already-typed values. Arguments that need contextual inference retain ordinary matching. Constructors, calls with `*args: *tuple[...]` signatures, keyword unpacks, or unresolved `ParamSpec` or `TypeVarTuple` parameters also retain their existing behavior.

pulls.title: [ty] Match alternative positional unpack lengths
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now consider alternative unpack lengths when matching non-generic calls to fixed positional parameters. This accepts a typed argument between two unknown-length unpacks when the arguments can fill the parameters in order:

```python
def f(a: int, b: int, c: str, d: int, e: int): ...

def call(before: list[int], text: str, after: list[int]):
    f(*before, text, *after)
```

The matcher checks complete arrangements against argument order, required tuple elements, defaulted parameters, and explicit keyword assignments. When no arrangement succeeds, we use the existing matching and diagnostics. Calls exceeding the 65,536-state limit also use the existing matcher.

Alternative matching is limited to scalar literals and references to already-typed values, including callbacks. Lambdas, collection literals, call expressions, class references, and `TypeForm` parameters retain ordinary matching and contextual inference.

Generic calls, constructors, calls with variadic positional parameters, and calls with keyword or tuple-union unpacks retain their existing behavior.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/3649.

pulls.title: [ty] Fix notebook cell lookups after cells with cell magics
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now resolve notebook requests to the correct Python cell after cells containing a cell magic such as `%%bash`. Previously, hovering `x` in an `x = 1` cell could show the type of `z` from the following `z = "zz"` cell.

The server identifies cells by their position in the notebook, but `Notebook::cell_range` used that index to look up offsets among Python cells only. We now translate between those indices and return no range for cells excluded from the Python source. Semantic token and folding range requests for those cells return no results instead of falling back to the whole notebook.

pulls.title: [ty] Clamp notebook cell positions to the end of the cell
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now clamp notebook request positions to the end of the requested cell's content. For example, `(0, 1)` in an empty cell resolves to `(0, 0)`, consistent with the [LSP rule for character offsets beyond the end of a line](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/gh-pages/_specifications/lsp/3.17/types/position.md).

Previously, we converted positions against the concatenated notebook source, allowing a position past the end of a cell to resolve into a later cell. Hovering just past an empty cell could show the type of `x` from a following `x = 1` cell, and an inlay hint request could return hints from the next cell.

We now bound position conversion by the cell's content range, excluding its synthetic separator newline. If the cell has no source range, we return `None` instead of falling back to the start of the notebook.

pulls.title: [ty] Fix panic on completions past the end of a notebook's last cell
pulls.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a completion panic in a notebook with an empty last cell.

To analyze a notebook, we combine its Python cells into one source string, adding a newline after each cell:

```text
First cell:       "x = 1"       at offsets 0..5
Empty last cell:  ""            at offsets 6..6
Combined source:  "x = 1\n\n"  at offsets 0..7
```

We parse the cells separately, but the resulting module describes the combined source. Previously, we ended that module at offset 6, where the empty cell's content ends. Position conversion uses the combined source, so a request for character 1 of the empty cell can resolve to offset 7. That is the end of the source, but it was outside the module's range. Looking up the completion position then panicked with `Range is not contained within root`.

We now give the module the range 0..7, as we would when parsing the same source as a whole. This makes positions at the end of the combined source safe to look up. #29307 separately corrects position conversion so the same request resolves to offset 6, the end of the requested cell's content.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4687.

pulls.title: [ty] Add diagnostics when modifying frozen pydantic fields
pulls.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to Ruff/ty! To help us out with reviewing, please consider the following:

- Does this pull request include a summary of the change? (See below.)
- Does this pull request include a descriptive title? (Please prefix with `[ty]` for ty pull
  requests.)

-->

## Summary
Add support for frozen Pydantic fields.

The previous diagnostics was limited to frozen models and did not support individually frozen fields.


```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Model(BaseModel):
    x: int = Field(frozen=True)

m = Model(x=1)

# Old
m.x = 5 # No diagnostic
# New
m.x = 5 # error: [invalid-assignment]
```

<!-- What's the purpose of the change? What does it do, and why? -->

## Test Plan
New mdtests

pulls.title: [ty] Reuse normalization when extending unions
pulls.body:
## Summary

We reuse normalization results while constructing chains of PEP 604 unions, including unions of specialized generic classes:

```python
class A[T]: ...
class B[T]: ...
class C[T]: ...

Alias = A[int] | B[int] | C[int]
```

Previously, extending a union rebuilt its left-hand prefix and compared the existing members with one another again. `UnionBuilder::build_normalized` now returns a `NormalizedUnion`, which retains the resulting type and its construction policy. `add_normalized` can seed an empty builder from that result without repeating those comparisons. If the program or construction policy differs, or the destination already contains members, it uses ordinary union construction.

pulls.title: [ty] Fix deadlock when requests arrive before workspace configuration
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now process ready worker actions before replaying requests deferred while waiting for `workspace/configuration`. Previously, a large deferred request burst could fill both bounded queues: workers waited to enqueue responses while the main loop waited to enqueue more jobs, leaving the server unresponsive.

This extends the existing priority for worker actions to deferred requests while preserving client message order. The regression test queues 64 hover requests before replying to configuration, then checks that all requests and a subsequent hover receive responses.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4707.

pulls.title: [ty] Experiment with binding wrapped methods
pulls.body:
Apply [python/typeshed#16515](https://github.com/python/typeshed/pull/16515) to the vendored `functools` stubs to measure its effect on ty's ecosystem diagnostics. The change adds `__get__` overloads so functions decorated with `functools.wraps` or passed as the wrapper to `functools.update_wrapper` bind their first argument when accessed as methods.

The overloads also model callable objects passed as the wrapper as descriptors even when they have no `__get__`. In that case, ty can treat them as bound methods even though instance access leaves them unchanged at runtime, leading to false positives.

[ty] More return type inference preparations

pulls.title: [ty] Compare nominal instances directly in unions
pulls.body:
## Summary

We compare nominal instance payloads directly when checking for duplicate
union elements. This avoids going through the full `Type` comparison in union

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve known module owners when uv reports unknown IDs
pulls.body:
[uv#22395](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22395) proposes reporting module owners for installed distributions outside the resolution. If one shares a module with a resolved package, ty currently discards both owners. This can cause ty to reject the metadata and disable dependency checks for the project.

This PR filters out unknown owner IDs while retaining owners present in the resolution. If no owners remain, it keeps an empty entry so the module does not inherit its parent’s owner.

After filtering, ty can attribute a module to a single known owner even when an unknown installed distribution also provides it.

pulls.title: [ty] Prepare mdtests for return type inference
pulls.body:
## Summary

This PR prepares our mdtests for return type inference. For example, we had some definitions like
```py

```
which were supposed to be used in `if flag()` tests of ambiguous truthiness. However, with return type inference, ty would understand that this function returns `None`, which is falsy.

I'm pulling this out so as to reduce the diff on the upcoming return type inference PR.

## Test Plan

Tested by running the return type inference implementation against these changes.

pulls.title: [ty] Skip truthiness merge calls for non-intersection types
pulls.body:
## Summary

We skip the truthiness merge helper when the incoming type isn't an
intersection. The helper already returns `None` for these types, so this avoids
unnecessary calls in union normalization.

pulls.title: [ty] Leave room for later positional arguments when unpacking a variable-length argument
pulls.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a bug where unpacking something like `*args` would eat up all the remaining positional parameters. Because of this, if you passed another explicit argument *after* the unpack (like `f(*args, x)`), the type checker thought there was no space left for `x`. This caused false positive `too-many-positional-arguments` or `invalid-argument-type` errors.

To fix this, we updated the logic in `bind.rs`. Now, if a function doesn't have a variadic parameter, we count how many explicit positional arguments come after the unpack and reserve room for them so everything fits properly.

Part of: astral-sh/ty#3649.

pulls.title: [ty] Avoid constructing nominal complements
pulls.body:
## Summary

When checking whether a nominal complement is a subtype of another nominal instance, we currently construct an intersection and run the general relation check. This can succeed only if either operand is the dedicated `object` instance, so we can answer directly when the negation cache is empty.

pulls.title: [ty] Reuse alias searches in union normalization
pulls.body:

When preserving aliases, we currently walk the incoming type again for every existing union member. Keep that result for the current type and clear it whenever normalization replaces the type.

We still repeat walks through `NewType` instances and constructors, since their bases come from semantic queries.

pulls.body:

pulls.title: [ty] Inline nominal instance class accessors
pulls.body:

The nominal instance class accessors are small matches used throughout union simplification. Mark them `#[inline(always)]` so we can avoid the function calls and expose those matches to the caller.

pulls.title: [ty] Avoid repeated equality checks in union normalization
pulls.body:
