pulls.title: Allow suppressing unmatched-suppression-comment (RUF104)
pulls.body:
﻿## Summary

`RUF104` (`unmatched-suppression-comment`) could not be suppressed with `ruff:ignore`, `ruff:file-ignore`, or a `ruff:disable` block, and the comment that tried to suppress it was then reported by `RUF100` as unused.

`check_suppressions` now collects the `disable` comments that suppressed a diagnostic but have no matching `enable`, then asks `check_rule(RUF104, ...)` whether that report is itself suppressed. A suppressed `RUF104` is not emitted, and the suppressing comment is marked used, so `RUF100` does not report it. Candidates are collected before any of them is checked, so order does not matter. `# ruff:disable[T201, RUF104]` on one comment can suppress its own `RUF104`. A lone unused `# ruff:disable[RUF104]` is still reported by `RUF100`. `# noqa: RUF104` and a file-level `# ruff: noqa: RUF104` are outside this change.

Closes #29106.

pulls.title: Mark FURB103 unsafe when write() may not match the mode
pulls.body:
﻿## Summary

FURB103's fix stayed safe even when the value passed to `write()` did not match the open mode. `open(..., "w")` truncates the file before `write()` runs, so a type error leaves an empty file. `Path.write_text` / `Path.write_bytes` reject the value before opening the file, so applying the fix changes that behavior.

The fix is safe only when the argument is known to be `str` for text mode or `bytes` for binary mode. That is inferred from the expression itself (literals, f-strings, and similar) or, for a name, from a single binding's annotation or assignment (`typing::is_string` / `is_bytes`), for example `def foo(x: str)`. A mismatched type, or an unknown type (unannotated parameter, call result such as `str(1)`, `.encode()`), is unsafe. A comment inside the `with` block still makes the fix unsafe, as before.

Fixes #26920.

## Test Plan

﻿## Summary

UP040, UP046, and UP047 offered a fix that dropped `TypeVar(..., **{...})` unpacked keyword arguments, because those arguments cannot be represented on a PEP 695 type parameter. The diagnostic is still reported. If any referenced type variable was defined with unpacked keyword arguments, including a mix of ordinary and unpacked type variables, no fix is offered.

`expr_name_to_type_var` now returns a `TypeVarLookup` (`Unresolved` / `Resolved` / `UnpackedKeywords`) so callers do not look the name up twice. UP040 and UP047 change from `FixAvailability::Always` to `Sometimes`. RUF053 shares that lookup and also withholds its fix in this case. That RUF053 path was not given its own test.

Fixes #27008.

## Test Plan

pulls.title: [ty] Combine constraints from repeated ParamSpecs
pulls.body:
This PR implements support for specifying multiple ParamSpecs in the signature which the constraint solver combines using union or intersections.

For example, in the following case two specializations of the same ParamSpec gets combined into a union given that `P` is in covariant position:

```py
def choose[**P](left: Callable[P, None], right: Callable[P, None]) -> Callable[P, bytes]: ...

def left(x: int, /) -> None: ...
def right(x: str, /) -> None: ...

# ((x: int, /) -> bytes) | ((x: str, /) -> bytes)
reveal_type(choose(left, right))
```

And in the following example they get combined into an intersection given that `P` is in contravariant position:
```py
def choose[**P](left: Callable[Callable[P, None], None], right: Callable[Callable[P, None], None]) -> Callable[P, bytes]: ...

def consume_int(callback: Callable[[int], None]) -> None: ...
def consume_str(callback: Callable[[str], None]) -> None: ...

# ((int, /) -> bytes) & ((str, /) -> bytes)
reveal_type(choose(consume_int, consume_str))
```

Currently, there are two main issues that I've highlighted in the review comments with the relevant regression tests.

pulls.title: Unwrap stringized annotations in PYI036
pulls.body:
﻿## Summary

PYI036 (`bad-exit-annotation`) read the raw annotation expression. A quoted annotation such as `tb: "TracebackType | None"` was always reported, including annotations produced by the TC004 quote-annotations fix. The check now unwraps a stringized annotation with `match_maybe_stringized_annotation` before validating it, in all three places the rule looks:

- positional `__exit__` / `__aexit__` parameters, including `"object"` and `"Unused"`
- the variadic `*args` check
- the `@overload` check

Fixes #27755.

## Test Plan

`cargo test -j 8 -p ruff_linter --lib -- flake8_pyi::tests::rules::rule_badexitannotation` → 2 passed (`PYI036.py` and `PYI036.pyi`). The snapshot was generated once with `INSTA_UPDATE=always` and then confirmed with `INSTA_UPDATE=no`. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` (toolchain 1.97) passed.

Not run: the rest of the Ruff tests, clippy, mdtest, the ecosystem check, and `cargo dev generate-all`.

  `wrangler workflows instances list my-workflow --json`

  The JSON output carries raw values rather than a serialisation of the formatted view: ISO timestamps instead of locale-formatted dates, plain status strings instead of emojified labels, and no presentation-only derived fields.

##### Minor Changes

- [#​15454](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15454) [`dbbb795`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/dbbb795c47ff663857b605b484c63730e1e3ff45) Thanks [@​jamesopstad](https://redirect.github.com/jamesopstad)! - Move binding utilities into `@cloudflare/workers-utils`

  Binding conversion, printing, and local-development validation are now exported from `@cloudflare/workers-utils` so they can be shared by Wrangler, the Cloudflare Vite plugin, and other consumers.

  The corresponding exports have been removed from `@cloudflare/deploy-helpers`. Consumers should import them directly from `@cloudflare/workers-utils` instead.

  Wrangler's `unstable_printBindings` API now accepts the bindings and an options object instead of five positional parameters.

- [#​15353](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/15353) [`87a7acf`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/87a7acf197629f5bf16bb38a2e411dc6c21339e0) Thanks [@​pombosilva](https://redirect.github.com/pombosilva)! - Add `--date-start` and `--date-end` filters to `wrangler workflows instances list`

  You can now narrow an instance listing to a creation-time window:

  `wrangler workflows instances list my-workflow --date-start 2026-01-01 --date-end 2026-01-31`

  Either flag can be used independently. Both accept an ISO 8601 date or timestamp and are normalised to UTC before being sent, so a date-only value such as `2026-01-01` works as well as a full `2026-01-01T13:00:00Z`. The bounds are inclusive and compose with the existing `--status` filter.

Miniflare, its shared CLI and container dependencies now use granular `@cloudflare/workers-utils` entry points instead of loading the package barrel, reducing the raw Wrangler and Miniflare artifacts by 6.16 MiB (31.4%) and 1.06 MiB (22.9%) respectively without changing runtime behavior or installed dependencies.

  Telemetry events include a `currentAgentSkillsInstalled` property, and computing it can query the GitHub API. The lookup used to start before the telemetry permission was checked, so users who opted out via `WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, or `send_metrics` in their Wrangler config still triggered network requests on behalf of telemetry. The dispatcher now checks the permission first and only performs the lookup when telemetry is enabled.

pulls.title: [ty] Make lazy type traversal explicit
pulls.body:
## Summary

All remaining callers of `any_over_type` and `find_over_type` use the old `false` behavior: walk stored nested types without evaluating lazy attributes. The flag no longer varies between callers, so we remove it and make that traversal the fixed behavior of both helpers.

Analyses that need lazy attributes now choose them explicitly. Visitors override the methods for the types they need to expand; for example, the recursion check explicitly visits alias values, protocol members, `TypedDict` fields, type-variable attributes, and `NewType` bases. Specialized alias searches can still compose the general helper: `any_over_type_expanding_aliases` uses it to walk stored types and explicitly recurses into alias values.

This preserves existing traversal behavior while removing the visitor-wide lazy-attribute switch and the shared search modes.

pulls.title: [ty] Simplify mapped intersections through aliases
pulls.body:
## Summary

Builds on #29152.

We now simplify mapped intersections through aliases without expanding the alias unless a simplification changes the result. For example:

```python
from typing import Literal
from ty_extensions import Intersection, Not

type Minus[T, U] = Intersection[T, Not[U]]
type Boolean = bool
type TrueLiteral = Literal[True]

def f(x: Minus[Boolean, TrueLiteral]):
    reveal_type(x)  # Literal[False]
```

Previously, we revealed `Boolean & ~Literal[True]`. The alias was retained to avoid unfolding recursive types, but that hid the boolean from the normal simplification rule.

Intersection construction still expands unions, nested intersections, and enum complements so it can distribute and flatten them. The inner builder now inspects the underlying types when applying simplification rules, including truthiness, enum exclusions, constrained type variables, and gradual generics. Unchanged aliases retain their identity. This removes the separate lists of positive and negated alias shapes that could be preserved.

pulls.title: [ty] Avoid hangs on recursive tuple aliases in positive intersections
pulls.body:
## Summary

Builds on #29057. We now handle recursive tuple aliases specialized into positive intersections without hanging:

```python
from collections.abc import Iterable
from typing import Any, assert_type
from ty_extensions import Intersection

type WithIterable[T] = Intersection[Iterable[Any], T]
type A = tuple[WithIterable[A], ...]

def f(x: A):
    reveal_type(x)  # tuple[WithIterable[A], ...]
    assert_type(x[0], WithIterable[A])
```

Previously, mapping the intersection unfolded `A` again after its mapping had completed. Each reconstruction could introduce another copy of the tuple, so even revealing `x` would not terminate.

We extend the existing alias-preservation mode to positive elements. The builder retains aliases to non-`object` nominal instances on the positive side and continues to apply its sign-specific rules for negated aliases. Aliases that expose `object` or set operations still expand, and ordinary intersection redundancy checks still run. The regressions cover both alias syntaxes, the returned element type, and an invalid assignment.

pulls.title: [ty] Inspect dynamic content through finite recursive types
pulls.body:
## Summary

We preserve negative tuple-pattern narrowing when an element contains a finite recursive protocol or `TypedDict`. The dynamic-content check follows fixed, permuted, and normalized type arguments until an exact type repeats. Growing or unresolved recursion remains conservative, as do recursive references that introduce `Any` or `Unknown`.

The recursion analysis includes protocol methods and retains the bindings of generic methods and property accessors. Bounds, constraints, and defaults are inspected explicitly when checking dynamic content, including for redundant-cast diagnostics.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve checks for recursive descriptor setter types
[ty] Promote tuple lengths based on the outer element types
pulls.body:
## Summary

We normally infer `list[tuple[int, ...]]` for `[(1,), (1, 2)]`, allowing tuples of other lengths to be added later. This tuple-size promotion applies to tuple literals; tuple types supplied by annotations or other expressions retain their existing lengths.

The check that preserves those lengths currently searches for tuples anywhere inside an element's type. This incorrectly blocks promotion when the tuple appears inside a generic type argument, a callable's return type, or a protocol member:

```python
class Box[T]: ...

def example(box: Box[tuple[int, str]]) -> None:
    values = [(1,), (1, 2), box]
    reveal_type(values)
    # Before: list[tuple[int] | tuple[int, int] | Box[tuple[int, str]]]
    # After:  list[Box[tuple[int, str]] | tuple[int, ...]]
```

The `Box` is not a tuple, so its type argument should not prevent us from widening the two tuple literals. We replace this use of `any_over_type` with a check for whether the element itself may be a tuple. The check still follows aliases, unions, type-variable bounds, and `NewType` bases that can describe a tuple value, while skipping nested type arguments and members.

pulls.title: [ty] Validate Generic and Protocol arguments directly
pulls.body:
## Summary

We validate the arguments to `Generic[...]` and `Protocol[...]` directly. An invalid argument can contain a `TypeVarTuple` in one of its members, but that does not make it a valid type parameter. We now report the invalid argument instead of treating it as an unsupported variadic form.

This also avoids expanding unrelated members and recursive bounds while validating a class's generic parameters.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve literal types when consuming dictionary literals
pulls.body:
Dictionary literals currently promote their keys and values even when consumed immediately, so a lookup table such as `{"A": "Alpha", "B": "Beta"}[letter]` returns `str` and can fail a literal-union return annotation. Preserve literal types when indexing or iterating over a dictionary literal, or calling its `keys()`, `values()`, or `items()` method directly.

This is just expanding to literal dictionaries an existing pattern we already supported for literal lists and tuples.

Recover key and value unions from the already-inferred elements, including literal `**` unpacking. Stored dictionaries, nested mutable containers, and saved bound methods keep their ordinary mutable types. Dictionary lookups return the union of the value types.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4680

## Test plan

Mdtests cover immediate lookups with literal and nonliteral keys, lookup-table returns, invalid key types, direct iteration and dictionary views, stored views, comprehension and destructuring targets, literal and arbitrary mapping unpacking, duplicate keys, and mutation through nested containers and saved bound methods.


## Ecosystem report

For head `a0cb267abac45badbcd2329ee5f5bafad339dbba`, all ten stable diagnostic changes are expected: four false-positive argument errors removed, two useful redundancy warnings added, and four existing messages made more precise. No regression found; CI passed. See the [full ecosystem analysis](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29145#issuecomment-6024243441) for minimized examples and source links.

pulls.title: [ty] Pass inferable typevars to satisfiability checks
pulls.body: This addresses a review comment from astral-sh/ruff#28996. The `is_always_satisfiable` and `is_never_satisfiable` methods now take in an `inferable` set, and perform the sat check relative to that set of inferable typevars. This ensures that these checks are consistent with whatever solves we perform on the constraint set.

pulls.title: [ty] Thread provenance through constraint set relations
pulls.body: Constraint set relations now take a `ConstraintProvenance` parameter, allowing the provenance of the constraint set to be chosen upon construction, instead of a forcing a second pass to create a set of validity constraints. See https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28909#discussion_r4196400566.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve conditional dictionaries during keyword unpacking
pulls.body:
When a conditional dictionary is unpacked into a call, ty can lose the keys and values associated with each branch. For example, `f(**({"x": 1} if flag else {}))` can miss that one branch does not provide a required `x`.

Preserve each dictionary literal branch as a separate argument list, including for fresh, unannotated function-local dictionaries used only for keyword unpacking and with one reaching assignment. Within the expansion limit, check each combination and combine the return types when all branches match. Use the branch-specific bindings for generic constructors, `ParamSpec` forwarding, known calls, and inference for initially empty dictionaries.

Dictionary alternatives share the existing 256-case argument expansion limit, including through `ParamSpec` forwarding, partial applications, and property accessors.

In a reduced replay of 27 ecosystem reproducers and one direct-local control, the change removes 9 diagnostics across 6 cases. Ohm and the repository toolchain produced the same results.

Stacked on [#29138](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29138).

pulls.title: [ruff] Use `regex-lite` for WebAssembly formatter builds
pulls.body:
## Summary

Introduce `ruff_regex` with target-specific backends: `regex-lite` for WebAssembly and `regex` for native builds. Upstream integration enables testing of the shared syntax subset and backend compatibility, which downstream dependency patches alone cannot enforce.

Scope is limited to `ruff_python_formatter`. Downstream consumers requiring migrations in other crates, including lint crates, can open issues or contribute PRs. Each migration must address unsupported syntax and semantic differences between the backends.

Replace `\p{any}*` with `(?s:.*)`. WASM uses ASCII whitespace and case folding, preserving Unicode matching remains open for discussion.

- Related to #21827.
- Related to #20845
- Close #29139

## Test Plan

- Existing formatter tests pass: 51 unit tests and 376 fixture tests.
- Clippy passes for `ruff_regex` and `ruff_python_formatter` with `--all-targets --all-features`.
- Repository hooks pass.
- A temporary formatter-only harness verified matching base WASM, head WASM, and head native outputs across 571 fixture configuration variants.

Measurements from the formatter-only WASM harness:

| Measurement | Base | Head | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| WASM binary size | 3,217,471 bytes | 2,327,638 bytes | −27.7% |
| Ordinary Python (`pypinyin.py`) | 27.3 ms | 27.9 ms | +2.0% |
| Docstring-heavy (`docstring_code_examples.py`) | 139.3 ms | 147.7 ms | +6.1% |

Both builds use identical release settings with `wasm-opt` disabled. Timings are medians of five rounds of 200 formatting calls, after 100 warmup calls per build, with alternating base/head order. Measurements use Node.js 24.16.0 on ARM64 macOS. The ordinary workload uses default options and the docstring workload enables `docstring_code`.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve local dictionary contents during keyword unpacking
pulls.body:
Unpacking a local dictionary into a call can produce a false `invalid-argument-type` diagnostic. In this contrived example, ty compares the dictionary's `str | int` value type against `optional: bool`, even though the dictionary has no `optional` key:

```python
def pair(x: int, y: str, optional: bool = False) -> None: ...

def valid() -> None:
    options = {"y": "two", "x": 1}
    pair(**options)
```

The call now passes.

Preserve explicit string keys and each value's type from a fresh, unannotated function-local dictionary literal when a single assignment reaches the call and every use of the name directly unpacks keyword arguments. Use this information for call binding, overload selection, `ParamSpec` forwarding, and signature help.

Annotations, aliases, mutations, captures, and ambiguous assignments continue to use ordinary dictionary inference. Reflective mutation through `locals()`, `vars()`, or frames is not modeled.

Adapted from @tamird's [prototype](https://github.com/tamird/ruff/commit/d885fa047cc261f5a4279efbb5c504db5c94da14). Related to [astral-sh/ty#3792](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/3792).

pulls.title: [ruff] Use 16 KiB code-signature pages for ARM64 macOS releases
pulls.body:
The macOS release signing workflow uses 4 KiB code-signature pages, increasing the number of code slots macOS hashes during signature verification. Update the shared signing action and use its pinned `rcodesign` build to apply 16 KiB pages to ARM64 executables in wheels and release archives; x86_64 signatures continue to use 4 KiB pages.

Depends on #29079 and astral-sh/github-actions#8.

pulls.title: [ty] Infer defaults for absent closed TypedDict keys
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now infer only `None` or the supplied default when `get` looks up a key that cannot exist in a closed `TypedDict`:

```python
from typing import reveal_type
from typing_extensions import TypedDict

class Person(TypedDict, closed=True):
    name: str
    age: int

def example(person: Person, key: str):
    reveal_type(person.get("email"))
    # Before: str | int | None
    # After:  None

    reveal_type(person.get("email", b"missing"))
    # Before: str | int | Literal[b"missing"]
    # After:  Literal[b"missing"]

    reveal_type(person.get(key))
    # Still: str | int | None
```

Since `Person` is closed, it cannot contain an `"email"` key, so these calls always return the default. Previously, we included the declared fields' types even when the key was definitely absent. We retain the broader result for an arbitrary `str`, which could refer to a declared field. This also works through saved `get` method references.

Adapted from @tamird’s [original change](https://github.com/tamird/ruff/commit/773bc39f514a3ccccb20714006f262f2c0c7e01b).

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve final attribute restrictions on composite types
pulls.body:
ty can allow assignment to or deletion of a `Final` instance attribute when the receiver is a union or has been narrowed through a protocol. Another member of the composite type can make the attribute appear writable.

In this contrived example, ty previously accepted the assignment because `Mutable.value` is writable. With this change, ty reports `invalid-assignment` because the receiver could be a `Fixed` instance:

```python
from typing import Final

class Fixed:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.value: Final[int] = 1

class Mutable:
    value: int = 1

def update(either: Fixed | Mutable) -> None:
    # previously this was fine, but with this PR:
    either.value = 2  # error: [invalid-assignment]
```

Check the members of unions and positive intersection components for `Final` restrictions. Assignment checks also follow type aliases, so an aliased union member retains the restriction.

A class can still assign to its own `Final` attribute through `self` in `__init__`, even when `self` is narrowed through a protocol. If several union members prohibit the same assignment, ty reports one error and stops checking rather than producing duplicate errors.

Adapted from @tamird’s [original change](https://github.com/tamird/ruff/commit/cf8a56c1a9ae9e6f71863546fb638f01ad4cb6b2).

pulls.title: [ty] Validate type-variable defaults through aliases
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now reject type-variable defaults that reference an out-of-scope or later type variable through an alias, using the same scope and ordering rules as direct references.

```python
type Items[T] = list[T]

def outer[T]():
    def inner[U = Items[T]](): ...  # Error: T is bound in an outer scope
```

The check preserves valid defaults whose alias arguments are unused or erased by specialization, and ignores variables bound by nested callable signatures. We also apply the outer-scope check to parameter lists used as `ParamSpec` defaults.

Builds on #29132 and uses its free-type-variable traversal, including its existing limitation for occurrences exposed only after growing recursive alias references.

pulls.title: [ty] Validate free type variables in ClassVar annotations
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now reject `ClassVar` annotations whose types contain free type variables hidden by aliases or captured in protocol members and `TypedDict` fields. We also allow `Self` in generic classes and type variables bound by a nested callable's own signature.

```python
from typing import ClassVar

type Items[T] = list[T]

class Container[T]:
    values: ClassVar[Items[T]]  # Error: ClassVar cannot contain type variables
```

The traversal expands alias values so unused arguments and arguments erased by specialization do not cause errors. It tracks callable bindings and treats type-variable bounds and defaults as metadata.

We follow finite recursive specializations, including cases where a protocol member or `TypedDict` field exposes a variable only after the first specialization. The shared recursion analysis distinguishes fixed outer variables from captures whose binding definitions also participate in the recursion. Occurrences beyond growing or unresolved recursive references can still remain undiagnosed; an incomplete search does not produce an error.

We reuse completed searches under the same callable bindings to avoid repeatedly traversing shared types, such as those in Pydantic's `CoreSchema`. An incomplete recursive search cannot supply a cached result.

Builds on #29155.

pulls.title: [ty] Infer empty collection branches from nonempty literals
pulls.body:
For `["x"] if flag else []`, ty currently infers `list[Unknown]`. Similarly, `{"x": 1} if flag else {}` is inferred as `dict[Unknown, Unknown]`.

Infer the nonempty branch first when the other branch is an empty literal of the same kind. This lets the empty branch use its peer’s type as context, so both branch orders infer `list[str]` and `dict[str, int]` for these examples.

Adapted from @tamird's [original change](https://github.com/tamird/ruff/commit/7914a959af9d50fed9b741052d0f02d49d3689fa).

pulls.title: Clarify PR labeling and update Ruff changelog exclusions
pulls.body:
## Summary

Ruff's changelog can include PRs labelled `release` or `playground`. Configure Rooster to exclude PRs with those labels, bringing Ruff's ignored-label list closer to ty's: ty already excludes both. Ruff's Documentation section remains unchanged.

Replace the obsolete `docstrings` label mapping with `docstring` in Rule changes. Rule changes precedes Formatter, so a PR with both `docstring` and `formatter` labels will appear under Rule changes unless an earlier section also matches.

Update the PR guidance in `AGENTS.md` to inspect label descriptions, skip archived labels, and choose labels appropriate to the PR's content. For ty PRs, apply the `ty` label when possible.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve type-variable dependencies through aliases
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now infer `int` for `get_parameter(distribution)` in this stub example, instead of retaining the helper method's type parameter in the result:

```python
from typing import Protocol, assert_type

type ParameterType[T] = T

class HasParameter[T](Protocol):
    def parameter(self) -> T: ...

class Distribution[T]:
    def parameter[S](self: Distribution[S]) -> ParameterType[S]: ...

def get_parameter[T](distribution: HasParameter[T]) -> T: ...

distribution: Distribution[int]
# Before: type-assertion-failure; inferred S@parameter | int
# After: passes; inferred int
assert_type(get_parameter(distribution), int)
```

The dependency on `S` is hidden inside `ParameterType[S]`. We now include type variables in alias values when collecting constraint dependencies, so we can remove the helper method's type parameters from the inferred result. An alias such as `type Alias[T] = T` preserves the dependency on `T`; an unused alias argument does not create one. Runtime `TypeAliasType` objects remain distinct from the types their aliases denote.

When recursive alias expansion stops, we retain dependencies found in its arguments and mark constraint dependency information as incomplete. We also retain these variables when deciding whether a type parameter belongs to a function or to a generic callable it returns, so a recursive parameter annotation does not incorrectly move the variable into the returned callable's scope.

pulls.title: [ty] Enforce nonempty generic contexts
pulls.body:
Make `GenericContext` nonempty and use `None` when no type variables remain. This prevents equivalent nongeneric signatures from comparing differently after binding `Self` or applying a specialization.

Preserve explicit generic declarations' precedence and extend the existing test to cover an empty `Generic[()]` base.

Refer to https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/28828#discussion_r4203717285 for more context.

pulls.title: [ty] Invalidate dependency metadata when environments change
pulls.body:
`Project::dependency_metadata` resolves Python environments inside a Salsa query without tracking those inputs. This can leave invalid-environment, missing-environment, and environment-mismatch diagnostics stale after an environment changes.

Store the selected environment's resolution result in `ProgramSettings` and track uv's environment directory through Salsa. Resolve uv's canonical path whenever the query runs so it observes symlink changes even when uv metadata is unchanged.

After a failed selection, retain the last usable environment for watching and recovery, and preserve the checking program's search paths. Dependency metadata reports the current environment error.

Fixes astral-sh/ty#4604.

pulls.title: [ty] Narrow tuple unions through truthiness and type checks
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now narrow unions of tuples when an element is checked for truthiness or with `isinstance`, `issubclass`, or `TypeIs`. Eliminating an alternative also narrows the tuple’s other elements, preserving the relationship between a tag and its associated value. For example, checking a boolean literal tag selects the corresponding callable signature in either branch.

We reuse the tuple-union filtering used by equality checks and register the containing tuple as a possible narrowing target for call predicates. We keep uncertain alternatives and skip filtering for non-literal or out-of-bounds indices. `TypeGuard` checks retain their existing behavior.

For truthiness checks and calls, we skip the additional tuple narrowing if the expression contains an assignment (`:=`). Evaluating the expression can replace the tuple after it has been read. This conservatively includes harmless assignments to other names; a TODO test records that limitation.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4674.

pulls.title: [flake8-print] Preserve trailing comments in the T201/T203 fix
pulls.body:
### Summary

Follow-up to #29105, from the same bug class: the T201 (`print`) and T203 (`pprint`) fixes deleted the statement's full lines, so a comment sharing the line with the call was deleted along with it:

```python
print("debug: cache stats")  # TODO: remove after metrics dash ships
```

was fixed to an empty line. When the statement ends its line with only a comment following it, and the default statement deletion would take the full-lines path, the fix now deletes up to the start of the comment instead, retaining the comment and its indentation:

```python
# TODO: remove after metrics dash ships
```

The interception is gated on the same conditions `delete_stmt` uses to choose its full-lines branch, so every other shape is untouched: a lone child (`if debug: print("dbg")  # keep me`) still becomes `pass  # keep me` rather than an empty block, semicolon-chained lines keep their existing deletion, and continuation lines are unaffected. The trailing-comment detection reuses the established `trailing_comment_start_offset` helper (as PIE790 and PYI013 already do); `is_lone_child` in `fix/edits.rs` is made `pub(crate)` for the branch-order check rather than duplicated.

Suggested labels: `bug`, `fixes` (I don't have permission to apply them).

### Test Plan

- Fixture cases added to `T201.py` and `T203.py` (a debug print and a pprint with realistic trailing comments). The updated snapshots show all 14 commented diagnostic lines across both fixtures retaining their comments, including the new cases.
- `cargo test -p ruff_linter`: 2834 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p ruff_linter --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `prek` on the changed files: all hooks pass.
- End-to-end with a debug build, covering all four branch shapes — lone child with a trailing comment (`pass  # TODO: ...`), two prints on one line with a trailing comment (`pass  # keep`), a semicolon-chained statement with a comment (`x = 1;   # inline note`), and a lone child without a comment. Comments were retained in every case and all outputs parse as valid Python.

pulls.title: [flake8-pyi] Preserve trailing comments in the PYI012 fix
pulls.body:
### Summary

The PYI012 (`pass-in-class-body`) fix deleted the `pass` statement's full lines, so a comment sharing the line with the `pass` was deleted along with it:

```pyi
class C:
    x: int
    pass  # keep me
```

was fixed to:

```pyi
class C:
    x: int
```

When the `pass` ends its line with only a comment following it, the fix now deletes up to the start of the comment instead, retaining the comment and its indentation:

```pyi
class C:
    x: int
    # keep me
```

All other cases still use the default statement deletion. This follows the same approach as PYI013 (`ellipsis-in-non-empty-class-body`), the sibling rule, which already preserves trailing comments via `trailing_comment_start_offset`; the same helper is reused here.

Suggested labels: `bug`, `fixes` (I don't have permission to apply them).

### Test Plan

- No fixture changes were needed: all six commented `pass` lines in `PYI012.pyi` were already covered, and their snapshot entries now show the comment retained instead of deleted.
- `cargo test -p ruff_linter`: 2834 passed.

pulls.title: [ty] Fix signature help for unmatched arguments
pulls.body:
Signature help can highlight an unrelated parameter when an argument does not bind to an overload. In a contrived example with overloads `f(a: int, *, b: int)` and `f(a: int, *, c: int)`, placing the cursor on `2` in `f(1, b=2)` also highlights `c` in the second overload.

pulls.title: Isolate daily fuzz issue creation from the fuzzer
pulls.body:
The daily parser-fuzz job runs third-party build dependencies and has permission to write issues. Move issue creation into a separate job so code run during fuzzing cannot access the issue-write token. Pass the generated report as an artifact for the issue body. If the report is unavailable or creating that issue fails, the reporting job attempts to create a fallback issue linking to the workflow run.

ty's daily fuzz workflow also uses Ruff's py-fuzzer. The corresponding change in [astral-sh/ty#4671](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/pull/4671) keeps the reporting steps aligned so they can be compared and maintained together.

pulls.title: [ty] Refactor call argument representation
pulls.body:
Call matching handles starred arguments in several places, with each consumer interpreting the inferred source type separately. This makes it difficult to carry more precise unpacked values through call analysis.

Represent positional, keyword, and unpacked arguments as distinct `CallArgument` variants. Move sequence and keyword unpacking into the argument types, and share those operations across matching, overload expansion, and partial application. Keep one entry per source argument so diagnostics and signature help can refer to the original call.

This is a behavior-preserving refactor that prepares for literal unpacking. The overload regression test covers a variable-length argument matched to different arities before a keyword argument.

pulls.title: [flake8-print] Preserve trailing comments in the T201/T203 fix
pulls.body:
### Summary

Follow-up to #29105, from the same bug class: the T201 (`print`) and T203 (`pprint`) fixes deleted the statement's full lines, so a comment sharing the line with the call was deleted along with it:

```python
print("debug: cache stats")  # TODO: remove after metrics dash ships
```

was fixed to an empty line. When the statement ends its line with only a comment following it, and the default statement deletion would take the full-lines path, the fix now deletes up to the start of the comment instead, retaining the comment and its indentation:

```python
# TODO: remove after metrics dash ships
```

The interception is gated on the same conditions `delete_stmt` uses to choose its full-lines branch, so every other shape is untouched: a lone child (`if debug: print("dbg")  # keep me`) still becomes `pass  # keep me` rather than an empty block, semicolon-chained lines keep their existing deletion, and continuation lines are unaffected. The trailing-comment detection reuses the established `trailing_comment_start_offset` helper (as PIE790 and PYI013 already do); `is_lone_child` in `fix/edits.rs` is made `pub(crate)` for the branch-order check rather than duplicated.

Suggested labels: `bug`, `fixes` (I don't have permission to apply them).

### Test Plan

- Fixture cases added to `T201.py` and `T203.py` (a debug print and a pprint with realistic trailing comments). The updated snapshots show all 14 commented diagnostic lines across both fixtures retaining their comments, including the new cases.
- `cargo test -p ruff_linter`: 2834 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p ruff_linter --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `prek` on the changed files: all hooks pass.
- End-to-end with a debug build: standalone `print(x)  # note` keeps the comment; `if debug:` lone-child gets `pass  # keep me`; `a = 1; print("semi")  # note` keeps the comment. All three outputs parse as valid Python.

pulls.title: [pylint] Preserve trailing comments in the PLR1711 fix
pulls.body:
### Summary

Fixes #28861.

The PLR1711 (`useless-return`) fix deleted the return statement's full lines, so a comment sharing the line with the `return` was deleted along with it:

```python
def f():
    print(5)
    return None  # keep me
```

was fixed to:

```python
def f():
    print(5)
```

When the `return` is alone on its line and only a comment follows it, the fix now deletes up to the start of the comment instead, retaining the comment and its indentation:

```python
def f():
    print(5)
    # keep me
```

All other cases — multi-line returns, semicolon-chained lines, lines with leading statements — still take the default statement deletion, which already handles them. The new path only fires when the trailing line content after the statement is whitespace followed by `#`, so a semicolon after the `return` (where a leading `;` would make the result invalid Python) still falls through to the default deletion.

Suggested labels: `bug`, `fixes` (I don't have permission to apply them).

### Test Plan

- Added two fixture cases to `useless_return.py`: a `return None` with a trailing comment (the issue's shape) and a bare `return` with a trailing comment. The snapshot shows the comment retained in both, and all five pre-existing comment cases now retain their comments instead of deleting them.
- The trailing-comment detection reuses the established `trailing_comment_start_offset` helper (as PIE790 and PYI013 already do), rather than a rule-local one-off.
- `cargo test -p ruff_linter`: 2834 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p ruff_linter --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `prek` on the changed files: all hooks pass.
- End-to-end check with a debug build `--fix`ing a file containing `return  # comment` and `return None  # comment`: comments retained, output parses as valid Python.

pulls.title: [`flake8-pyi`] Accept stringized annotations in `bad-exit-annotation` (`PYI036`)
pulls.body:
## Summary

`PYI036` was flagging valid `__exit__` / `__aexit__` signatures whenever an annotation was quoted, e.g.:

```py
def __exit__(self, typ: type[BaseException] | None, exc: BaseException | None, tb: "TracebackType | None") -> None: ...
```

A quoted annotation means the same thing to a type checker as the unquoted one. This often comes from `TC004` with `quote-annotations = true`, which quotes annotations that reference imports only available under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`. In that setup, the two rules conflict.

This PR makes the rule parse the string and check it the same way as an unquoted annotation, using `Checker::match_maybe_stringized_annotation`, in all three places it inspects annotations:

- star-args (`*args: "object"`)
- positional parameters of non-overloaded `__exit__` / `__aexit__`
- positional parameters of overloaded `__exit__` / `__aexit__`

A quoted annotation that would be invalid unquoted (e.g. `"type[Exception] | None"`) is still reported.

<!-- Closes #XXXX -->

## Test Plan

Added an mdtest at `crates/ruff_linter/resources/mdtest/flake8-pyi/bad-exit-annotation.md` covering:

- quoted valid annotations (plain, `types.`-qualified, and `object`), which should produce no diagnostic
- quoted invalid annotations, which are still reported
- quoted references to `TYPE_CHECKING`-only imports (the `TC004` interaction)
- quoted star-args, including a snapshot of the existing fix
- quoted annotations in overloads, both valid and invalid

Have `py-fuzzer` write a Markdown issue body with minimized reproducers and the tested binary's build commit, and use that body in the scheduled parser-fuzzing workflow. pulls.title: [ty] Preserve escape sequences in mdtest snapshots
pulls.body:
## Summary

mdtest snapshot filtering can treat Python escape sequences as Windows paths. For example, a diagnostic containing `b"\x41"` can be recorded as `b"/x41"`.

This change enables accurate snapshots for diagnostics containing Unicode escapes such as `\u200b` in [the PR adding the `non-exhaustive-match` rule](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29053).

For inline and standalone snapshots, we now recognize a candidate as a path if it exists in the test or vendored filesystem, or if it is under a test search root and its components do not resemble escapes. This preserves escapes such as `\x41`.

To reduce ambiguity, we also reject explicitly named mdtest files with path components that begin with escape-like text (such as `src/x64.py`), or whose paths contain whitespace or snapshot delimiters (such as `src/foo bar.py`). Single-letter components such as `n` are allowed.

## Limitations

Path normalization is best-effort: rendered diagnostic text still does not always perfectly distinguish paths from other text. A perfect distinction is not really necessary for mdtests, however, since we can just avoid writing tests that exercise these pathological cases. But, for example:

- A string literal can still be mistaken for a path in some situations. For example, a test file named `n/mod.py` creates the directory `/src/n` under the default workspace root. A diagnostic containing `value: int = "src\n"` can then be snapshotted as `value: int = "src/n"`.
- A path mentioned in a diagnostic that does not exist in the test filesystem can be left unnormalized if a component resembles a Python escape. For example, `src\x64.py` may remain unchanged instead of becoming `src/x64.py`.

## Test plan

Existing tests in `ty_python_semantic` already demonstrated our over-eager normalization of non-paths. These snapshots are corrected as part of this PR.

pulls.title: [ty] Fix type variable inference for final class objects
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now infer `T = Closed` when matching a callback that accepts `type[Closed]` against `Callable[[type[T]], None]`, including when `Closed` is final. Previously, we inferred the class literal and rejected the callback.

```python
from typing import Callable, final, reveal_type

def solve[T](callback: Callable[[type[T]], None]) -> T:
    raise NotImplementedError

@final
class Closed: ...

def takes_closed(cls: type[Closed]) -> None: ...

reveal_type(solve(takes_closed))  # Closed, previously <class 'Closed'>
```

Final class objects project exactly to their instance types because they cannot have subclasses. We now preserve that distinction for both class literals and specialized generic classes, removing the redundant special case for final upper bounds.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4664.

pulls.title: [`flake8-type-checking`] Fix lazy imports with multiple names (`TC001`, `TC002`, `TC003`)
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29068.

On Python 3.15+, `TC001`, `TC002`, and `TC003` fall back to a `TYPE_CHECKING` block for imports with multiple names, even when every name is used only for typing. This change allows the whole statement to become lazy in that case. For example, when both names are used only in annotations:

```diff
-from collections.abc import Collection, Iterable
+lazy from collections.abc import Collection, Iterable
```

Adding `lazy` affects every name in the statement. Checking only the name that triggered a diagnostic could also defer a runtime-used import or change an import excluded by an exemption, suppression, or disabled rule. The fix therefore counts eligible, unsuppressed typing-only imports for each statement and allows a multi-name statement to become lazy only when that count matches its number of names. Unused names do not count either, so they also prevent the whole-statement conversion. In those cases, the existing fix moves only the qualifying names into a `TYPE_CHECKING` block.

The count combines first-party, third-party, and standard-library imports because one statement can contain names covered by different rules, such as `import app, vendor, pathlib`. The existing Python-version, scope, `try`-statement, and `ban-lazy` checks still apply. Single-name imports retain their existing behavior.

The lazy fix inserts one `lazy ` prefix without rebuilding the statement, preserving aliases, parentheses, and comments. Ruff's fix application deduplicates identical edits from multiple diagnostics on the same statement. The fix remains unsafe because deferring an import can change runtime behavior.

## Test Plan

- Added mdtests for multiple names across all three rules, mixed categories, aliases, parentheses, comments, and relative imports, plus fallback cases and lazy-import policy interactions. Generated diagnostic snapshots were reviewed.
- All 56 Ruff mdtest files pass with snapshot updates disabled.
- All 9,333 workspace tests pass; file-watcher tests are skipped.
- CLI checks verify that unsafe fixes insert exactly one prefix, safe fixes preserve the source, repeated fixes are unchanged, and mixed runtime/typing imports retain the `TYPE_CHECKING` fallback.
- Workspace Clippy passes for all targets and features with build warnings denied. Documentation generation and repository hooks pass.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve tuple shapes when slicing NewTypes
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now infer `tuple[int, str]` for slices of tuple-based `NewType`s like this one:

```python
from typing import NewType

MyTuple = NewType("MyTuple", tuple[int, str, None])

def example(value: MyTuple) -> tuple[int, str]:
    return value[:2]
```

Previously, we fell back to the general `__getitem__` signature and inferred `tuple[int | str | None, ...]`. We now apply tuple slicing to the `NewType`'s concrete base, returning a plain tuple with the sliced element types.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4632.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve tuple subclass identity during type expansion
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now recognize exhaustive class patterns over tuple subclasses, including `NamedTuple`. For example, this function no longer produces an `invalid-return-type` error:

```python
from typing import NamedTuple

class Point(NamedTuple):
    x: bool

def handle(value: Point) -> int:
    match value:
        case Point():
            return 42
```

Tuple expansion now intersects each expanded tuple with the original subclass, preserving its class identity during reachability analysis and overload resolution.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4659.

pulls.title: [ty] Improve display of string literal types that include unicode characters or double quotes
pulls.body: ty currently displays some string-literal types with Rust-style escapes that are invalid in Python. For example, a string containing U+200B is shown as `Literal["\u{200b}"]`; Python uses `\u200b` for this character. ty also always uses double quotes, so a value such as `'a"b'` is shown as `Literal["a\"b"]`. This PR uses Python-style escapes and prefers double quotes, switching to single quotes when the value contains double quotes but no single quotes. It escapes default-ignorable characters, which can be invisible, and combining marks that would otherwise attach to an opening quote or escape sequence. For example, `"\u0301"` is displayed as `Literal["\u0301"]`, preventing the mark from attaching to the opening quote. It also escapes certain characters in parts of a string that are not in [Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC)][NFC], so visually identical values such as `"é"` and `"e\u0301"` are displayed distinctly as `Literal["é"]` and `Literal["e\u0301"]`. The following table compares the displayed types for the string values `'a"b'`, `"\u200b"` (a zero-width space), `"é"`, `"e\u0301"`, and `"\u0301"`, targeting Python 3.12: The `"\u200b"` and `"\u0301"` columns use screenshots because some checkers display an invisible zero-width space or leave a standalone combining mark unescaped, which can render differently across browsers. | Checker | `'a"b'` | `"\u200b"` | `"é"` | `"e\u0301"` | `"\u0301"` | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | ty on `main` | `Literal["a\"b"]` | | `Literal["é"]` | `Literal["e\u{301}"]` | | | ty with this PR | `Literal['a"b']` | | `Literal["é"]` | `Literal["e\u0301"]` | | | mypy 2.4.0 | `Literal['a"b']` | | `Literal['é']` | `Literal['é']` | | | Pyrefly 1.3.2 | `Literal['a"b']` | | `Literal['é']` | `Literal['é']` | | | Pyright 1.1.414 | `Literal['a"b']` | | `Literal['é']` | `Literal['é']` | | | Zuban 0.10.0 | `Literal['a"b']` | | `Literal['é']` | `Literal['é']` | | | Pycroscope 0.5.0 | `Literal['a"b']` | | `Literal['é']` | `Literal['é']` | | This rendering will also be used by the proposed [`non-exhaustive-match` rule](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/29053), whose diagnostics show uncovered values and their types. [NFC]: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr15/#Norm_Forms

pulls.title: [ty] Report conflicting attribute declarations across class body and methods
pulls.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to Ruff/ty! To help us out with reviewing, please consider the following:

- Does this pull request include a summary of the change? (See below.)
- Does this pull request include a descriptive title? (Please prefix with `[ty]` for ty pull
  requests.)
- Does this pull request include references to any relevant issues?
- Does this PR follow our AI policy (https://github.com/astral-sh/.github/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md)?
-->

## Summary

<!-- What's the purpose of the change? What does it do, and why? -->
Closes astral-sh/ty#206.

With this change ty now reports `conflicting-declarations` when attribute declarations in methods don't agree with class body declarations:

```py
class C:
    x: int

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.x: str = ""  # error: [conflicting-declarations]
```

The check runs as part of the post-inference pass of class definitions. For each implicit attribute it collects the annotated declarations in the class body and all methods and compares them for equality. This also means that declaring a narrower type is not possible and will lead to an error:
```py
class Parser:
    tokens: list[str] | None = None

    def parse(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.tokens: list[str] = text.split()  # error: [conflicting-declarations]
```

### Limitations

I am using the declarations at the end of a method for comparisons. This allows redeclaration of symbols but it hides the fact that for a method with multiple returns there can be multiple declarations active at the end of a method. I added a markdown test for this (`crates/ty_python_semantic/resources/mdtest/attributes.md:455-470`):

```py
class C:
    def set_value(self, flag: bool) -> None:
        if flag:
            self.x: int = 1
            return
        self.x: str = "a"  # TODO: error: [conflicting-declarations]

    def reset_value(self, flag: bool) -> None:
        if flag:
            self.y: int = 1
            return

    def clear_value(self) -> None:
        self.y: str = ""  # TODO: error: [conflicting-declarations]
```



## Test Plan

<!-- How was it tested? -->
I added markdown tests including snapshots and added tests marked with TODO for the current limiations.

pulls.title: [`flake8-bugbear`] Avoid false positive for frozen dataclass defaults (`B008`)
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29071.

`function-call-in-default-argument` (`B008`) flags frozen-dataclass constructors used as parameter defaults even when every field is immutable:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Foo:
    val: bool = True

def bar(foo: Foo = Foo()) -> None: ...
```

A frozen dataclass whose fields are all immutable is safe to share as a default argument — `frozen=True` prevents field reassignment, and the immutable field types prevent mutation of the contents — so this is a false positive. Because `frozen=True` only provides *shallow* immutability, the exemption is deliberately narrow: only frozen dataclasses whose fields are all immutable are recognized.

## Approach

`ArgumentDefaultVisitor` (in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/flake8_bugbear/rules/function_call_in_argument_default.rs`) reports any call in a default argument unless it is a known mutable constructor (`list`/`dict`/`set`), a known immutable constructor (`str`/`int`/`tuple`/...), or an immutable `NewType` call. Frozen-dataclass instantiations matched none of these.

Added `is_immutable_dataclass_instantiation` in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/ruff/helpers.rs`, next to the existing `dataclass_kind` / `is_frozen_dataclass` helpers used by `RUF008`/`RUF009`. It resolves the callee to its class definition, requires a stdlib `@dataclass(frozen=True)`, then requires every field's annotation to be immutable (`is_immutable_annotation`) and every field default (when present) not to be a mutable expression (`is_mutable_expr`), skipping `ClassVar` fields. Any unresolvable step returns `false`, so it errs toward flagging.

This is wired in as an additional guard in `ArgumentDefaultVisitor`, and the shared dataclass helpers are exposed crate-wide (`pub(crate)`).

Notes:
- Scoped to stdlib `@dataclass(frozen=True)`; `attrs` field detection is out of scope.
- B008 runs eagerly, so the class must be defined before the function in source order for the exemption to apply; a forward reference falls back to the previous "flag it" behavior.
- `RUF009`'s existing (broader) frozen-dataclass exemption is left unchanged; this PR is scoped to `B008`.

## Test Plan

Added `crates/ruff_linter/resources/test/fixtures/flake8_bugbear/B008_frozen_dataclass.py` covering:

- frozen + immutable fields → no diagnostic
- frozen + mutable field (`items: list`) → diagnostic
- non-frozen → diagnostic
- `ClassVar` field excluded
- nested-immutable `tuple[int, ...]` field → no diagnostic
- immutable annotation with a mutable default (`val: int = []`) → diagnostic

`cargo test -p ruff_linter --lib flake8_bugbear` passes (77 tests).

pulls.title: [flake8-bugbear] Detect redundant built-in exception subclasses (`B014`)
pulls.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29073.

B014 detects exact duplicate exceptions, such as `(ValueError, ValueError)`, but previously missed cases where one builtin exception is already covered by another, such as `(OSError, TimeoutError)`.

This extends B014 in preview mode to recognize known builtin exception inheritance. It uses semantic resolution so that shadowed or rebound names are not incorrectly treated as builtin exceptions.

## Implementation Notes

- Uses semantic resolution rather than relying only on exception spellings.
- Keeps the expanded behavior behind preview, preserving stable B014 behavior.
- Defers analysis when an enclosing function exists so later function-local bindings are known, while preserving class and module sequential lookup.
- Limits inheritance checks to builtin exceptions; user-defined and imported exception hierarchies remain out of scope.
- Preserves B025's existing syntactic duplicate detection across separate handlers.

## Test Plan

- All 97 flake8-bugbear tests passed, including existing B014/B025 tests and the added regression cases.
- Verified stable and preview behavior through automated tests.
- Covered reversed tuple ordering, transitive inheritance, unrelated exceptions, and combinations of exact duplicates with hierarchy redundancy.
- Covered function-local shadowing, nested classes with enclosing-function shadowing, class-body sequential lookup, and initialized builtin imports.
- Formatting, relevant Clippy checks, touched-file `prek`, generation, and `git diff --check` passed.

## AI Assistance

I originally ran into this while enabling stricter lint rules in one of my Python projects. I expected B014 to catch cases where one exception was already covered by another, so I investigated further, reproduced the behavior, and opened #29073 after looking through Ruff's implementation and the existing related discussion.

I used Codex (6.1 Sol) as a development aid while learning Ruff's Rust codebase, working through the implementation, and thinking through edge cases and regression tests. I reviewed the resulting changes myself, manually tested the behavior, and made sure I understood the semantic-resolution, scoping, preview, and deferred-analysis decisions involved.

I take responsibility for the contribution and am happy to adjust the implementation based on maintainer feedback.

## Acknowledgement

Thanks @ntBre for the guidance on #29073, especially the suggestion to keep this expansion behind preview.

pulls.title: [ty] Share parameter-default inference between functions and lambdas
pulls.body:
## Summary

Superseded by #29025, which now preserves the evaluation context of lambda defaults through its expression queries and includes this PR's regression coverage.

We already infer defaults for named functions separately from their annotations. Call checking only needs to know whether a parameter has a default, and evaluating its value while building the signature can re-enter the decorated function's own signature inference.

This PR extends that separation to lambdas, using a shared inference region for each parameter default. Previously, reading a lambda default could infer its entire enclosing scope, causing recursive decorators to grow nested container types without converging.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4613.

pulls.body:
We grow the stack on demand while inferring expressions, avoiding stack overflow on long expression chains. This preserves contextual inference and expression caching for each operand. The CLI regression now checks a 5,000-term addition and verifies its inferred literal value.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/4104.

pulls.body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to Ruff/ty! To help us out with reviewing, please consider the following:

  requests.)
- Does this pull request include references to any relevant issues?

-->

## Summary

Inside a class body, `flake8-builtins` reports a `for`, `with ... as`, or `:=` target that shadows a builtin, but A001 does not. The A001 call site skipped every stored name in class scope because A003 handles class attributes, but A003 only considers assignment and annotation bindings, so those other binding kinds were reported by neither rule. The class-scope skip now applies only to the binding kinds A003 handles, by checking the stored name's `BindingKind`. Attribute and method bindings in a class still go to A003, so there's no double-reporting.

This is the gap left after #20178, which I picked up because no pull request was opened for it.

Fixes #20179

## Test Plan

I have added new class-scope cases in the A001 fixture covering both the three bindings that now fire and the attribute and method bindings that stay silent, updated the snapshot with three new diagnostics, and ran the `flake8-builtins` tests, `clippy`, and `fmt`.

pulls.title: [ty] Improve narrowing after match patterns
pulls.body:
## Summary

When an unguarded class pattern only captures a definitely bound attribute, ty can treat it as matching every instance of that class. The next case should then exclude that class from the subject type, but ty previously retained it:

```python
from typing import reveal_type

class Base: ...

class Child(Base):
    value: int = 0

def process(subject: Base) -> None:
    match subject:
        case Child(value=captured):
            pass
        case _:
            reveal_type(subject)  # Before: Base; after: Base & ~Child
```

This change analyzes pattern success and failure recursively. It can also narrow attributes inspected by class patterns, fields inspected by `TypedDict` mapping patterns, and expressions in tuple or list display subjects such as `(value,)`. After a compound pattern fails, an inspected expression is narrowed only when every possible failure constrains it. For example, failure to match `(left, right)` against `(int(), int())` does not by itself narrow either element, since either could have failed.

Nested class patterns can also exclude matching shapes from variable-length tuples. For example, in a `match` over `tuple[Base, ...]`, a `[Child(value=_)]` case makes a later `[Child()]` case unreachable.

Fixes astral-sh/ty#4648.

pulls.title: [suspicious] Add `shared-clock-mock`
pulls.body:
Adds the preview `shared-clock-mock` rule. Patching a clock or sleep function on a shared module can affect unrelated threads or tasks, including when the target is qualified with the consuming module:

```python
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

from example import worker

sleep = Mock()
with patch.object(worker.time, "sleep", sleep):
    worker.retry()
```

Replace the consuming module's binding to keep the fake local:

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

from example import worker

sleep = Mock()
with patch.object(worker, "time", SimpleNamespace(sleep=sleep)):
    worker.retry()
```

We also flag patches of wall-clock, monotonic, and performance-counter readings, plus `asyncio.sleep`. The rule recognizes `patch`, `patch.object`, pytest-mock fixtures, and `monkeypatch.setattr`, including string targets and imported aliases.

Nested `.time` and `.asyncio` targets use a naming heuristic, so attributes that already hold private clocks can produce false positives. This limitation is documented and covered by an example with suppression by rule name. There is no automatic fix: replacements need to preserve the other attributes used by the consuming module.

pulls.title: [ty] Keep unresolved TypeIs targets provisional
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now terminate inference for recursive `TypeIs` calls like this one:

```python
from typing import reveal_type
from typing_extensions import TypeIs

class Container[T]: ...

def is_container[T](value: object, other: T) -> TypeIs[Container[T]]:
    return True

while True:
    if is_container(value, type(value)):
        value = value.__str__
    else:
        value = {value}
    reveal_type(value)
```

Previously, an unresolved `TypeIs` target could make the `else` branch appear unreachable. We now defer that narrowing until the target is known, preserving the recursive type and diagnostics in both branches.

Addresses https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/3837.

pulls.title: [ty] Pass generic context to call inference solver
pulls.body:
## Summary

We pass the call signature's generic context into `CallInference::solve`, which uses it to specialize contextual type arguments. This fixes the undefined `generic_context` compilation error introduced in #28903.

pulls.title: [ty] Preserve stdlib identity when search paths overlap
pulls.body:
## Summary

We now preserve the identity of standard-library stubs when a custom typeshed overlaps a first-party or extra search path. This fixes the module-identification error behind the dependency-cycle panic in https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/523.

The two configuration settings establish different import roots:

- `typeshed` selects the standard-library stubs to use instead of our bundled stubs. With `typeshed = "./typings"`, we look under `./typings/stdlib/`.
- `extra-paths` adds high-priority import roots for Python modules and stubs. With `extra-paths = ["./typings"]`, we search `./typings/` directly.

For example, a custom stub distribution can contain both additional modules and standard-library replacements:

```text
project/
├── main.py
├── ty.toml
└── typings/
    ├── device.pyi
    └── stdlib/
        ├── VERSIONS
        ├── builtins.pyi
        ├── typing.pyi
        └── pathlib.pyi
```

```toml
# ty.toml
[environment]
root = ["."]
typeshed = "./typings"
extra-paths = ["./typings"]
```

Here, `root` identifies our first-party import roots. An `import device` finds `typings/device.pyi` through the extra path, while `import pathlib` finds `typings/stdlib/pathlib.pyi` through typeshed. This overlapping layout, as used by the MicroPython stubs in #2819, remains supported.

The ambiguity arises when we identify a file we are already analyzing. Depending on the search root, the same `typings/stdlib/typing.pyi` file can have three names:

| Search root | Module name |
| --- | --- |
| `typings/stdlib/` | `typing` |
| `typings/` | `stdlib.typing` |
| The project directory | `typings.stdlib.typing` |

Previously, an earlier extra or first-party path could determine that identity, even when we originally found the file through a standard-library import. We then failed to recognize its builtin or typing definitions as having special behavior. In the reported case, inference followed paths that formed an unhandled dependency cycle and panicked. Losing that special handling can also produce incorrect types even when inference does not panic.

We now derive the identity of standard-library stub files from the configured stdlib root first: `builtins.pyi` is `builtins`, and `typing.pyi` is `typing`. This preserves the semantics needed to check ordinary Python code with the configuration above:

```python
from typing import Literal, reveal_type

def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b

reveal_type(add(1, 2))  # int
add(1, "2")  # invalid-argument-type

value: Literal[1] = 1
reveal_type(value)  # Literal[1]
```

We resolve the canonical name using normal precedence and Python-version availability, and verify that it selects the same file. If it is shadowed or unavailable, we do not fall back to an alias under an enclosing search path.

We also change how we handle an exact duplicate of the stdlib import root:

```toml
[environment]
root = ["."]
typeshed = "./typings"
extra-paths = ["./typings/stdlib", "./overrides"]
```

We now search `./typings/stdlib` only at the stdlib position, after the other extra paths and project roots. In this example, `overrides/pathlib.pyi` wins. The same applies when the stdlib directory appears in `root`.

Listing the stdlib directory in `extra-paths` or `root` no longer lets users:

- Give it priority over other extra paths or project roots.
- Import `.py` files from it through that entry.
- Import stubs that its `VERSIONS` file excludes for the configured Python version.

The configuration is still accepted, but code relying on those behaviors can break. The earlier `extra-paths = ["./typings"]` layout still supports additional stubs such as `device.pyi`. Runtime lookup is unchanged.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/523.

pulls.title: [ty] Intern inferred lambda signatures
pulls.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #29025.

We now intern inferred lambda signatures separately from their source identities. Lambdas with identical signatures share an explicit `CallableType`, allowing structural comparisons to reuse the existing relation cache. Inference and recursive references retain the source identities introduced in #29025.

Callable kind and deprecation metadata are preserved when resolving signatures. We retain the existing reflexivity rules, so identical gradual signatures are not incorrectly treated as subtypes of each other.

This does not recover the pandas regression in #29025. Five alternating fresh-process runs against `5176257`, using matched Linux x86_64 profiling CLI builds on pandas `19b0ecf`, had median runtimes of 30.33s before and 30.60s after (0.9% slower), with identical diagnostics. The three files that accounted for most of the original regression improved from 4.25s to 4.21s across three runs per version. Sharing the inferred signatures and comparison cache alone is insufficient for this workload.

pulls.title: [ruff] Add `mutable-type-annotation-in-frozen-dataclass` (RUF078)

Addresses #28221

Implements the rule for mutable-type-annotation-in-frozen-dataclass (Tentatively designated as RUF078).

Frozen dataclasses are record classes in Python that are meant to be immutable. As a result, declaring an attribute of a dataclass with a mutable type annotation (e.g. `list` or `dict`) is senseless and should be avoided.

pulls.title: [ty] Support go-to-{def,dec} for overloaded fns
